items.name: Definitions 11.1.1–11.1.2, Remark 11.1.3 and Example 11.1.4: shtukas with legs, global and local, in equal characteristic
items.statement: For a scheme S/𝔽_p, a rank-n shtuka on the curve X with legs x_1, …, x_m ∈ X(S) is a rank-n bundle ℰ on S ×_{𝔽_p} X with φ_ℰ : (Frob_S × 1)^*ℰ ≅ ℰ on S ×_{𝔽_p} X ∖ ⋃Γ_{x_i}. For X̂ ≅ Spf 𝔽_p[[T]] and an adic space S/Spa 𝔽_p with legs x_i ∈ X̂(S), a local shtuka is a rank-n bundle on S ×_{𝔽_p} X̂ with such a φ_ℰ meromorphic along ⋃Γ_{x_i} (Definition 5.3.5); this needs S ×_{𝔽_p} X̂ to have a good theory of bundles with the x_i closed Cartier divisors (e.g. S locally strongly noetherian or sousperfectoid). For S = Spa C, S × Spa 𝔽_p[[T]] is the open disc D_C, legs are topologically nilpotent x_i ∈ C, and one-leg shtukas at 0 are the σ-bundles of Hartl–Pink.
items.locator: Lecture 11, §11.1, Definition 11.1.1, Definition 11.1.2, Remark 11.1.3 and Example 11.1.4, pp. 90–91
items.note: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.2 (global multi-leg shtukas); RelativeFarguesFontaine and HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas HS2 cover equal-characteristic coefficient fields E = 𝔽_q((π)) alongside mixed characteristic.

items.name: Proposition 11.2.1: the analytic adic space S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p and its diamond S × Spd ℤ_p
items.statement: For S = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid of characteristic p with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p := Spa W(R⁺) ∖ {[ϖ] = 0} is an analytic adic space with (S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p)^♦ = S × Spd ℤ_p, hence a map |S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p| → |S|; this glues to any S ∈ Perf.
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0:integral-Y (𝒴_S = Spa(W_{O_E}(R⁺)) ∖ V([ϖ]) and FS II.1.2's 𝒴_S^♦ ≅ S × Spd O_E); FarguesFontaineDiamonds F1 for the fixed-field untilt product formula.

items.name: Proposition 11.3.1: sections of (S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p)^♦ → S are untilts, cut out by closed Cartier divisors
items.statement: For S ∈ Perf the following are naturally identified: sections of (S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p)^♦ → S; maps S → Spd ℤ_p; untilts S♯ of S. Given these, S♯ ↪ S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p is the inclusion of a closed Cartier divisor (𝒪 → 𝒪_{S♯} surjective with locally free kernel of rank 1).
items.note: RF2:untilts and RF2:integral-divisors (the primitive Cartier equation of an untilt, including characteristic-p untilts); FarguesFontaineDiamonds F4 ('Prove it is a closed Cartier divisor').

items.name: Definition 11.4.1 and Remark 11.4.2: mixed-characteristic shtukas
items.statement: For S ∈ Perf and legs x_1, …, x_m : S → Spd ℤ_p with closed Cartier divisors Γ_{x_i} : S_i♯ → S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p, a shtuka of rank n with these legs is a rank-n bundle ℰ on S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p with φ_ℰ : Frob_S^*(ℰ)|_{S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p ∖ ⋃Γ_{x_i}} ≅ ℰ|_{…}, meromorphic along the closed Cartier divisor Σ Γ_{x_i}.
items.note: HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas HS0/HS2 (Hecke stacks and local shtukas as modifications along the legs); Definition 23.1.1 is the G-version with bounds.

items.name: Definition 11.4.3 with Remarks 11.4.4 and 11.4.6: Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules
items.statement: For C/ℚ_p algebraically closed with θ : W(𝒪_{C♭}) → 𝒪_C, ker θ = (ξ), and φ = W(Frob), a Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module is a finite free W(𝒪_{C♭})-module M with an isomorphism φ_M : (φ^*M)[ξ^{-1}] ≅ M[ξ^{-1}] (analogous to Kisin's φ-modules over W(k)[[u]]). From Lecture 12 on the normalization is Frobenius-twisted (ξ replaced by φ(ξ), the leg at φ^{-1}(x_C)) for the crystalline comparison; Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze allow finitely presented M, finite free after inverting p, to accommodate torsion.
items.locator: Lecture 11, §11.4, Definition 11.4.3, Remark 11.4.4 and Remark 11.4.6, pp. 96–97
items.note: AInfCohomology AI.2 ('Construct finitely presented A_inf-modules M, finite free after p-inversion, equipped with phi-semilinear isomorphisms M[1/xi]→M[1/tilde-xi]').

items.name: Theorem 11.4.5 (Fargues): Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules are shtukas with one leg
items.statement: (M, φ_M) ↦ (ℰ, φ_ℰ) (restrict to Spa W(𝒪_{C♭}) ∖ {[ϖ] = 0}) is an equivalence between Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules over W(𝒪_{C♭}) and shtukas over Spa C♭ with one leg at the untilt C.
items.note: AI.2 plans Fargues' equivalence for finite free BKF modules with pairs (T, Ξ) 'using the analytic annulus/patching arguments of BMS1 §4'; the full five-category form is Theorem 14.1.1.

items.name: Theorem 12.1.1 with Remarks 12.1.2–12.1.3: the Hodge–Tate exact sequence of a p-divisible group over 𝒪_C
items.statement: For a p-divisible group G over 𝒪_C (C algebraically closed complete over ℚ_p) there is a natural short exact sequence 0 → Lie G ⊗_{𝒪_C} C(1) → T_pG ⊗_{ℤ_p} C → (Lie G*)* ⊗_{𝒪_C} C → 0 (Fargues), whose first map is α*_{G*} and second α_G: for f : ℚ_p/ℤ_p → G in T_pG, with dual f* : G* → μ_{p^∞}, α_G(f) is the image of 1 under the dual of Lie f* : Lie G* → Lie μ_{p^∞} ≅ 𝒪_C · (dt/t)^*. That α_G ∘ α*_{G*} = 0 is not formal (Tate treated the case over a DVR with perfect residue field).
items.locator: Lecture 12, §12.1, Theorem 12.1.1, Remark 12.1.2 and Remark 12.1.3, pp. 98–99
items.note: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0 ('Build the finite-level Hodge–Tate map using Cartier duality and differentials of characters') and T2 ('Prove the displayed Hodge–Tate exact sequence').

items.name: Definition 12.1.4 and Theorem 12.1.5 (Scholze–Weinstein, Theorem B) with Example 12.1.6 and Remark 12.4.7: p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C are pairs (T, W)
items.statement: Let {(T, W)} be the category of pairs of a finite free ℤ_p-module T and a C-subspace W ⊂ T ⊗_{ℤ_p} C. The functor G ↦ (T_pG, Lie G ⊗ C(1)) is an equivalence from p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C to {(T, W)}. (Example 12.1.6, corrected: for d = 1, the p-divisible group attached to (ℤ_p^h, W), W ∈ ℙ^{h−1}(C) a line, is isogenous to (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^{h−i} ⊕ G_i, G_i formal of height i and dimension 1, where i = dim H + 1 for the smallest ℚ_p-rational linear subspace H ⊂ ℙ^{h−1} containing W (printed 'i = dim_C H − 1', sourceIssues E1); those with special fibre G_h form Drinfeld's Ω^h(C) = ℙ^{h−1} ∖ ⋃ (ℚ_p-rational hyperplanes).) (Remark 12.4.7) {(T, W)} → {(T, Ξ)} is fully faithful, Ξ being the unique B_dR⁺-lattice with T ⊗ B_dR⁺ ⊂ Ξ ⊂ ξ^{-1}(T ⊗ B_dR⁺) whose image in T ⊗ C(−1) is W(−1).
items.locator: Lecture 12, §12.1, Definition 12.1.4, Theorem 12.1.5, Example 12.1.6 and Remark 12.4.7, pp. 99–106
items.note: Missing: no layer classifies p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0 constructs only the Hodge–Tate map). Routed with Theorems 14.1.1 (last part), 14.4.1–14.4.3, 15.2.3 and 17.5.2 as the Part II of PrismaticCohomology on prismatic Dieudonné theory, which the pending candidate from PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23 already plans in the quasi-syntomic generality.

items.name: §12.2: Spa A_inf, its special points x_k, x_L, x_{C♭}, x_C, the analytic locus 𝒴 and κ
items.statement: For A_inf = W(𝒪_{C♭}) with θ : A_inf → 𝒪_C, ker θ = (ξ), ξ = p − [p♭], p♭ = (p, p^{1/p}, …) ∈ 𝒪_{C♭}: Spa A_inf has a unique non-analytic point x_k; its complement 𝒴 carries a continuous κ : 𝒴 → [0, ∞] with κ ∘ φ = pκ; the points x_{C♭} (on p = 0, κ = 0), x_L (on [p♭] = 0, κ = ∞, residue field L = W(k)[1/p]) and x_C (cut out by p = [p♭]) are singled out, and 𝒴_I ⊂ 𝒴 denotes the locus κ ∈ I.
items.note: The Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 6.1–6.2 (A_inf, D(p) ∩ D([ϖ]), order-theoretic κ with κ(φv) = pκ(v)); RF0:integral-Y and RF0:annuli are the loci [ϖ] ≠ 0 and p[ϖ] ≠ 0. The part of 𝒴 near x_L is Proposition 13.1.1.

items.name: Definition 12.3.3: φ-modules over a ring or an adic space
items.statement: For a ring R with an endomorphism φ, a φ-module is a finite projective R-module M with M ⊗_{R,φ} R ≅ M (a φ-semilinear automorphism if φ is an automorphism); on an adic space with an endomorphism φ, a vector bundle ℰ with φ^*ℰ ≅ ℰ.
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB1 (bundles as finite projective modules on annuli with Frobenius descent).

items.name: Definition 12.3.1, Remark 12.3.2 and Theorem 12.3.4: the integral Robba rings and étale φ-modules over them
items.statement: R̃^int := 𝒪_{𝒴,x_{C♭}}, and R̃^{int,r} = H^0(𝒴_{[0,r]}, 𝒪) = A_inf⟨p/[p♭]^{1/r}⟩[1/[p♭]] = {Σ_{n ≥ 0}[c_n]p^n : c_n(p♭)^{n/r} → 0} for r > 0, with R̃^int = colim_{r → 0} R̃^{int,r}; R̃^int is a henselian DVR with uniformizer p, residue field C♭ and completion W(C♭), and φ induces R̃^{int,r} ≅ R̃^{int,r/p}. (12.3.4, Kedlaya–Liu 8.5.3) φ-modules over R̃^int, φ-modules over W(C♭) and finite free ℤ_p-modules are equivalent (base change, then φ-invariants).
items.locator: Lecture 12, §12.3, Definition 12.3.1, Remark 12.3.2 and Theorem 12.3.4, pp. 103–104
items.note: Missing: VB4 plans the rational equivalence between slope-zero bundles and E-local systems, but no layer plans the integral version over R̃^int or W(C♭). Routed as a source of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB4 with Propositions 22.3.2 and 22.6.1.

items.name: Proposition 12.3.5 and Corollary 12.4.1 with Remark 12.4.2: shtukas without legs, and removing one leg
items.statement: Shtukas over Spa C♭ with no legs are equivalent to φ-modules over R̃^int (hence to finite free ℤ_p-modules). For a shtuka (ℰ, φ_ℰ) over C♭ with a leg at φ^{-1}(x_C), its localization at x_{C♭} gives a shtuka (ℰ′, φ_{ℰ′}) without legs, and there is a unique φ^{-1}-equivariant isomorphism ι_ℰ : ℰ|_{𝒴_{[0,∞)} ∖ ⋃_{n ≥ 0} φ^n(x_C)} ≅ ℰ′|_{…} inducing the given identification at x_{C♭}, meromorphic along all φ^n(x_C) (likewise for several legs in characteristic 0).
items.locator: Lecture 12, §12.3, Proposition 12.3.5, Corollary 12.4.1 and Remark 12.4.2, pp. 104–105
items.note: Steps of the proof of Fargues' equivalence planned in AI.2 (BMS1 §4.3).

items.name: Definition 12.4.3 and Remarks 12.4.4–12.4.5: B_dR⁺ as a completed local ring of 𝒴, and the lattice Ξ of a one-leg shtuka
items.statement: B_dR⁺ := 𝒪̂_{𝒴,x_C}, the ξ-adic completion of W(𝒪_{C♭})[1/p], a complete DVR with residue field C and uniformizer ξ; θ extends to B_dR⁺ → C, B_dR = B_dR⁺[ξ^{-1}], and ξ^nB_dR⁺/ξ^{n+1} ≅ C(n); via φ, 𝒪̂_{𝒴,φ^n(x_C)} ≅ B_dR⁺ for all n. For a one-leg shtuka, ι_ℰ induces ℰ̂_{x_C} ⊗ B_dR ≅ T ⊗_{ℤ_p} B_dR (ℰ′ = T ⊗ 𝒪_𝒴), whose image Ξ is a B_dR⁺-lattice.
items.locator: Lecture 12, §12.4, Definition 12.4.3, Remark 12.4.4 and Remark 12.4.5, pp. 105–106
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory R06.1 (B_dR⁺, its filtration and B_dR), RF2:untilts ('Construct completion along a divisor, B_dR^+ and its localization B_dR'), AI.2 (the lattice Ξ).

items.name: Proposition 12.4.6: shtukas with one leg are pairs (T, Ξ)
items.statement: The functor above is an equivalence between shtukas over Spa C♭ with one leg at φ^{-1}(x_C) and pairs (T, Ξ) of a finite free ℤ_p-module T and a B_dR⁺-lattice Ξ ⊂ T ⊗_{ℤ_p} B_dR.
items.note: AI.2 ('Prove Fargues' equivalence for finite free BKF modules over algebraically closed C with pairs (T,Xi)').

items.name: Proposition 13.1.1, Remark 13.1.2, Theorem 13.1.3 and Example 11.2.2: 𝒴 is an adic space, and Kedlaya's noetherianity
items.statement: The analytic locus 𝒴 ⊂ Spa A_inf is an adic space (its rational localizations are sheafy); the same proof shows Spa W(R)[1/p] is an adic space for any discrete perfect ring R (with the p-adic topology). (Kedlaya, Noetherian properties of Fargues–Fontaine curves, 4.10) 𝒴_{[0,∞)} is strongly noetherian (not all of 𝒴: the local ring at x_L is highly nonnoetherian), and for a connected open affinoid Spa(R, R⁺) ⊂ Spa C♭ ×̇ Spa ℤ_p the ring R is a principal ideal domain; its maximal ideals correspond to the classical points, whose residue fields are the untilts of C♭.
items.locator: Lecture 13, §13.1, Proposition 13.1.1, Remark 13.1.2, Theorem 13.1.3 and Example 11.2.2, pp. 94–109
items.note: Missing: RF0:integral-Y proves sheafiness of 𝒴_S = Spa W(R⁺) ∖ V([ϖ]) by the direct-summand argument, but plans neither the part of 𝒴 near x_L nor strong noetherianity or the PID property. Routed as a source of RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0:integral-Y.

items.name: Theorem 13.2.1, Remark 13.2.2, Lemma 13.3.1 and Proposition 13.3.2: extending φ-modules over x_L
items.statement: For 0 ≤ r < ∞, restriction from φ-modules over 𝒴_{[r,∞]} to φ-modules over 𝒴_{[r,∞)} is an equivalence (Fargues–Fontaine 11.1.9, 11.1.13); so a shtuka over Spa C♭ with legs x_i and r > κ(x_i) extends uniquely to a bundle ℰ̂ on 𝒴 with φ_{ℰ̂} away from the legs. For r′ > r, restriction from 𝒴_I to 𝒴_{I ∩ [r′,∞]} is an equivalence of φ-modules (13.3.1); for r > 0 and a φ-module ℰ over 𝒴_{[r,∞]}, H^0(𝒴_{[r,∞]}, ℰ)^{φ=1} ≅ H^0(𝒴_{[r,∞)}, ℰ)^{φ=1} (FF 4.1.3, 11.1.12). Full faithfulness holds for any perfectoid C.
items.locator: Lecture 13, §13.2, Theorem 13.2.1, Remark 13.2.2, Lemma 13.3.1 and Proposition 13.3.2, pp. 109–110
items.note: AI.2 (the extension step of Fargues' equivalence, via BMS1 §4) and VB1 (Frobenius descent on annuli).

items.name: Theorem 13.4.1, Remark 13.4.2 and Definition 13.4.3: Kedlaya's theorem and the extended Robba ring
items.statement: (Kedlaya 2004) Every φ-module over 𝒴_{[r,∞)} is (M, φ_M) ⊗_L 𝒪_{𝒴_{[r,∞)}} for a φ-module (an isocrystal) over L = W(k)[1/p], so it extends to 𝒴_{[r,∞]}. Isocrystals over k are semisimple with simple objects M_λ, λ = d/h in lowest terms, of rank h with φ given by the companion matrix of p^d (Dieudonné–Manin). The extended Robba ring is R̃ = colim_r R̃_r, R̃_r = H^0(𝒴_{(0,r]}, 𝒪), with φ an automorphism of R̃; φ-modules over 𝒴_{(0,∞)}, over 𝒴_{[r,∞)} and over R̃ are equivalent.
items.locator: Lecture 13, §13.4, Theorem 13.4.1, Remark 13.4.2 and Definition 13.4.3, p. 111
items.note: VB2:classification (every bundle at a geometric point is a sum of O(λ), via the isocrystal functor), VB0 (Dieudonné–Manin classification) and VB1 (φ-modules on annuli).

items.name: Definition 13.5.1: the adic Fargues–Fontaine curve
items.statement: X_FF := 𝒴_{(0,∞)}/φ^ℤ (φ acts properly discontinuously since κ ∘ φ = pκ); φ-modules over 𝒴_{(0,∞)} are vector bundles on X_FF.
items.note: The Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 6 ('The adic Fargues–Fontaine curve', 𝒳 = 𝒴/φ^ℤ with wandering windows) and FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0.

items.name: §13.5: O(1), the graded ring P = ⊕ B^{φ=p^n}, A_crys and B_crys
items.statement: O(1) is the φ-module with trivial underlying bundle and φ_{O(1)} = p^{-1}φ; O(n) = O(1)^{⊗n} and P = ⊕_{n ≥ 0} H^0(X_FF, O(n)) with P_n = B^{φ=p^n} = (B⁺)^{φ=p^n}, where B = H^0(𝒴_{(0,∞)}, 𝒪) and B⁺ = H^0(𝒴_{(0,∞]}, 𝒪), by Proposition 13.3.2 (Fargues–Fontaine 4.1.3; printed 'by Proposition 13.2.1', sourceIssues E2). A_crys is the p-adic completion of the divided power envelope of A_inf → 𝒪_C, the A_inf-subalgebra of A_inf[1/p] generated by the ξ^n/n!, and B_crys⁺ = A_crys[1/p]; B^{φ=p^n} = (B_crys⁺)^{φ=p^n}.
items.note: RF3 (O(1) by Frobenius descent, O(n), the graded algebra of global sections), PadicHodgeTheory R06.1 (B_cris⁺) and AInfCohomology AI.0 (A_cris), VB1 (sections of O(n)).

items.name: Definition 13.5.2 and Theorem 13.5.3: the schematic Fargues–Fontaine curve
items.statement: X_FF := Proj P, with a distinguished point x_C (residue field C) from θ : B → C. (FF18) (1) X_FF is a regular noetherian scheme of Krull dimension 1, locally the spectrum of a PID; (2) X_FF ∖ {x_C} = Spec B_e, B_e = B_crys^{φ=1} a PID; (3) 𝒪̂_{X_FF,x_C} = B_dR⁺, so bundles on X_FF are B-pairs (M_e, M_dR⁺) (Berger); (4) closed points of X_FF correspond to characteristic-0 untilts of C♭ modulo Frobenius (via the residue field), so residue fields are algebraically closed nonarchimedean C′ with C′♭ ≅ C♭.
items.note: RF3 (Proj of the graded algebra and the analytic-to-schematic map), VB2:ampleness ('prove regular noetherian dimension-one structure of the schematic curve, its local principal-ideal properties and the closed-point description') and RF2:untilts (untilt divisors).

items.name: Theorem 13.5.4 and Corollary 13.5.5: classification of vector bundles on X_FF
items.statement: (FF18) M ↦ the bundle of the graded P-module ⊕_n (B_crys⁺ ⊗ M)^{φ=p^n} is a faithful, essentially surjective functor from isocrystals over k to bundles on X_FF, bijective on isomorphism classes; O(λ) is the image of M_{−λ}, of rank h and degree d for λ = d/h, compatible with O(n), and the λ_i of ⊕ M_{λ_i} are the slopes. Bundles semistable of slope 0 are equivalent to finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector spaces.
items.note: VB2:classification ('The isocrystal functor induces the source's bijection on isomorphism classes; it is not asserted fully faithful') with VB0 slope conventions, and VB4 (slope-zero bundles and local systems).

items.name: Theorem 13.5.6: GAGA for the curve
items.statement: Vector bundles on the adic curve X_FF and on the schematic curve X_FF are equivalent, via the map of locally ringed spaces X_FF^ad → X_FF (Kedlaya–Liu 8.7.7).
items.note: VB2:ampleness ('Compare bundles and cohomology on X_S and the Proj curve built in RF3').

items.name: Theorem 13.5.7: the Fargues–Fontaine curve is simply connected
items.statement: (Fargues–Fontaine, 8.6.1) X_{FF,ℚ̄_p} is simply connected: finite étale covers of X_FF are equivalent to finite étale ℚ_p-algebras; moreover finite étale covers of the adic and of the schematic curve are equivalent.
items.note: Missing: FarguesFontaineDiamonds F3 compares the finite étale sites of X_F and X_F^♦, and VB4 plans the slope-zero equivalence from which the result follows, but no layer states or proves simple connectivity; it is the input to Lemma 16.3.2 and the local Drinfeld lemma. Routed as a source of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB4.

items.name: Theorem 14.1.1 (Fargues), categories (1)–(5): the five descriptions of shtukas with one leg
items.statement: The following are equivalent: (1) shtukas over Spa C♭ with one leg at φ^{-1}(x_C) (bundles ℰ on 𝒴_{[0,∞)} with φ_ℰ meromorphic at φ^{-1}(x_C)); (2) pairs (T, Ξ), T finite free over ℤ_p and Ξ ⊂ T ⊗ B_dR a B_dR⁺-lattice; (3) quadruples (ℱ, ℱ′, β, T) with ℱ, ℱ′ bundles on X_FF, ℱ trivial, β : ℱ|_{X_FF ∖ {∞}} ≅ ℱ′|_{X_FF ∖ {∞}} and T ⊂ H^0(X_FF, ℱ) a ℤ_p-lattice; (4) bundles ℰ̃ on 𝒴 with φ_{ℰ̃} : (φ^*ℰ̃)|_{𝒴 ∖ φ^{-1}(x_C)} ≅ ℰ̃|_{…}; (5) Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules (finite free A_inf-modules M with φ_M : (φ^*M)[1/φ(ξ)] ≅ M[1/φ(ξ)]). The equivalence of (1)–(3) holds over general bases; the extensions to (4) and (5) use that the base is an algebraically closed field.
items.note: AI.2 (Fargues' equivalence, finite free BKF modules ↔ (T, Ξ), with 'the associated geometric modification comparison' on the curve) and RF4:vector-bundles (modifications along a divisor, category (3)). The restriction to p-divisible groups (last sentence of the theorem) is a separate item.

items.name: Theorem 14.2.1 (Kedlaya), Lemmas 14.2.3–14.2.4, Remark 14.2.5, Proposition 14.2.6 and Lemma 14.3.1: vector bundles on 𝒴 extend over Spa A_inf
items.statement: Finite free A_inf-modules are equivalent to vector bundles on 𝒴 (Kedlaya, Some ring-theoretic properties of A_inf, 3.6), the analogue of a 2-dimensional regular local ring. Algebraically, with 𝔪 the closed point, E ↦ E|_{Spec A_inf ∖ {𝔪}} is an equivalence (14.2.3), using that for a valuation ring V with residue field k and any V-submodule Λ ⊂ K^d, dim_k(Λ ⊗ k) ≤ d with equality iff Λ ≅ V^d (14.2.4). More generally, for K perfectoid of characteristic p with open bounded valuation subring K⁺ and pseudouniformizer ϖ, bundles on Spec W(K⁺) ∖ {p = [ϖ] = 0} are finite free W(K⁺)-modules (14.2.6). The proof uses 𝒴 = 𝒴_{[0,1]} ∪ 𝒴_{[1,∞]} with the rings S_1 = A_inf⟨[p♭]/p⟩[1/p], S_2 = A_inf⟨p/[p♭]⟩[1/[p♭]], S_12, S_1 ∩ S_2 = A_inf (Kedlaya–Liu 5.2.11(c)), and A_inf[p/[p♭]]^∧_p ≅ A_inf[p/[p♭]]^∧_{(p,[p♭])} (14.3.1). (Question 14.2.2 asks the same for G-torsors; answered by Theorem 21.2.2.)
items.locator: Lecture 14, §14.2, Theorem 14.2.1, Question 14.2.2, Lemma 14.2.3, Lemma 14.2.4, Remark 14.2.5, Proposition 14.2.6 and Lemma 14.3.1, pp. 116–120
items.note: AI.2's proof of Fargues' equivalence via BMS1 §4 uses exactly this extension from 𝒴 to Spec A_inf.

items.name: Theorem 14.1.1, last part, and Theorem 14.4.1: p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C are minuscule Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules
items.statement: Under Theorem 14.1.1, the full subcategories cut out by T ⊗ B_dR⁺ ⊂ Ξ ⊂ ξ^{-1}(T ⊗ B_dR⁺) in (2) are equivalent to p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C. Equivalently (14.4.1), p-divisible groups G over 𝒪_C are equivalent to finite free A_inf-modules M with a φ-linear isomorphism φ_M : M[1/ξ] ≅ M[1/φ(ξ)] such that M ⊂ φ_M(M) ⊂ φ(ξ)^{-1}M.
items.note: Missing, with Theorem 12.1.5; the pending prismatic Dieudonné Part II (Anschütz–Le Bras) recovers this over perfectoid rings, where admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystals are minuscule BKF modules.

items.name: Theorem 14.4.2 (Scholze–Weinstein, Theorem A): p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C/p and A_crys-modules
items.statement: Let A_crys be the p-adic completion of A_inf[ξ^n/n!], the universal p-adically complete PD thickening of 𝒪_C/p, and B_crys⁺ = A_crys[1/p]. The category of p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C/p embeds fully faithfully into the category of finite free A_crys-modules M_crys with an isomorphism φ_crys : M_crys ⊗_{A_crys,φ} B_crys⁺ ≅ M_crys[1/p].
items.note: Missing: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 plans Dieudonné theory over perfect fields; full faithfulness of crystalline Dieudonné theory over 𝒪_C/p is not planned. Routed with Theorem 12.1.5.

items.name: Theorem 14.4.3 and Corollary 14.4.4: the crystalline Dieudonné module of G_{𝒪_C/p} from its Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module
items.statement: For a p-divisible group G over 𝒪_C with Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module (M, φ_M), the crystalline Dieudonné module of G_{𝒪_C/p} is M ⊗_{A_inf} A_crys with φ_M ⊗ φ. Hence passage to the special fibre G ↦ G_k corresponds to (M, φ_M) ↦ (M ⊗_{A_inf} W(k), φ_M ⊗ φ) under Dieudonné theory over k (compare Kisin, and T. Liu for p = 2, over 𝒪_K).
items.note: Missing, with Theorem 12.1.5. The appendix proves 14.4.3 (announced there as 'Proposition 14.4.3'; sourceIssues E3) from Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze.

items.name: Theorem 14.6.1 and Proposition 14.7.2: the B_dR⁺-lattice in the p-adic cohomology of a proper smooth rigid space
items.statement: For a proper smooth rigid-analytic X over C there is a natural B_dR⁺-lattice Ξ ⊂ H^i_ét(X, ℤ_p) ⊗ B_dR, with Ξ ⊗_{B_dR⁺} C ≅ H^i_dR(X/C), and Ξ = H^i_dR(Y/K) ⊗_K B_dR⁺ when X = Y_C for Y proper smooth over a discretely valued K ⊂ C with perfect residue field (BMS 13.1, 13.8); it is crystalline cohomology relative to B_dR⁺ → C. For a proper smooth formal scheme 𝔛/𝒪_C with generic fibre X, H^i(𝔛_{𝒪_C/p}/A_crys) ⊗ B_dR⁺ ⊂ H^i_ét(X, ℤ_p) ⊗ B_dR is this lattice (BMS 14.5(i)).
items.locator: Appendix to Lecture 14, §14.6, Theorem 14.6.1 and Proposition 14.7.2, pp. 124–125
items.note: CohomologyComparisons CP.3 ('construct the canonical B_dR^+-valued deformation of de Rham cohomology … comparison after B_dR-inversion with p-adic étale cohomology') and AI.5.

items.name: Theorem 14.7.1 and Corollary 14.7.3: crystalline comparison and the Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module of H^i
items.statement: For a proper smooth formal scheme 𝔛/𝒪_C with generic fibre X there is a natural φ-equivariant isomorphism H^i(𝔛_{𝒪_C/p}/A_crys) ⊗ B_crys ≅ H^i(X_ét, ℤ_p) ⊗ B_crys (BMS 14.5(i)); with T_i = H^i(X_ét, ℤ_p)/torsion and Ξ_i from 14.6.1, the BKF module M_i attached to (T_i, Ξ_i) satisfies H^i(𝔛_{𝒪_C/p}/A_crys)[1/p] ≅ M_i ⊗_{A_inf} B_crys⁺ φ-equivariantly.
items.locator: Appendix to Lecture 14, §14.7, Theorem 14.7.1 and Corollary 14.7.3, pp. 125–126
items.note: AInfCohomology AI.4–AI.5 (A_cris specialization of RΓ_{A_inf}) and CohomologyComparisons CP.2 (rational crystalline comparison).

items.name: Theorem 14.9.1 and Corollary 14.9.2: the A_inf-cohomology of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze
items.statement: For a proper smooth formal scheme 𝔛/𝒪_C with generic fibre X there is a perfect complex RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) of A_inf-modules with φ-semilinear action and φ-equivariant isomorphisms RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) ⊗^L A_crys ≅ RΓ_crys(𝔛_{𝒪_C/p}/A_crys) and RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛) ⊗ A_inf[1/μ] ≅ RΓ(X_ét, ℤ_p) ⊗ A_inf[1/μ] (μ = [ε] − 1), recovering Theorem 14.7.1 over B_crys = A_crys[1/μ]; each H^i_{A_inf}(𝔛) is finitely presented, free after inverting p, and free if H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) is p-torsion free, in which case H^i(X_ét, ℤ_p) is too (BMS 1.8, 14.5(iii)). If H^j_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) is p-torsion free for j = i, i+1, i+2 then H^i_crys(𝔛_{𝒪_C/p}/A_crys) is p-torsion free and equals M_i ⊗_{A_inf} A_crys.
items.locator: Appendix to Lecture 14, §14.9, Theorem 14.9.1 and Corollary 14.9.2, pp. 127–128
items.note: AI.5 ('For smooth proper mathfrak X/O_C construct RΓ_Ainf … perfectness and finite presentation … BKF conditions'), AI.4 and CohomologyComparisons CP.1.

items.name: Proposition 14.8.1 (Faltings), Corollary 14.8.2 and Proposition 14.8.3: the crystalline comparison for p-divisible groups
items.statement: For a p-divisible group G over 𝒪_C with T = T_pG and crystalline Dieudonné module M_crys of G_{𝒪_C/p} there is a natural φ-equivariant isomorphism M_crys ⊗_{A_crys} B_crys ≅ T ⊗_{ℤ_p} B_crys under which M_crys ⊗ B_dR⁺ is the lattice Ξ (Faltings 1999). Hence, for the BKF module M of (T, Ξ), M_crys[1/p] ≅ M ⊗_{A_inf} B_crys⁺ (14.8.2), and this identifies the subobjects M_crys ≅ M ⊗_{A_inf} A_crys (14.8.3).
items.locator: Appendix to Lecture 14, §14.8, Proposition 14.8.1, Corollary 14.8.2 and Proposition 14.8.3, pp. 126–127
items.note: Missing, with Theorem 12.1.5: the proof of Theorem 14.4.3.

items.name: Propositions 14.9.3–14.9.4: reduction to formal abelian varieties
items.statement: For a formal abelian variety 𝔄 over 𝒪_C with generic fibre A and G = 𝔄[p^∞], under H^1(A_ét, ℤ_p) ≅ (T_pG)^* and H^1_crys(𝔄_{𝒪_C/p}/A_crys) ≅ M_crys(G_{𝒪_C/p})^*, the comparison isomorphisms of Theorem 14.7.1 and Proposition 14.8.1 correspond. For every p-divisible group G over 𝒪_C with Serre dual G* there is a formal abelian variety 𝔄 over 𝒪_C with 𝔄[p^∞] ≅ G × G* (and 𝔄 can be taken algebraic, keeping track of polarizations).
items.locator: Appendix to Lecture 14, §14.9, Proposition 14.9.3 and Proposition 14.9.4, p. 129

items.name: Theorem 15.1.1: G_{ℚ_p} × G_{ℚ_p} as a geometric fundamental group
items.statement: π_1((D̃*_{ℚ_p})^♦/ℚ_p^×) ≅ G_{ℚ_p} × G_{ℚ_p}, and for C/ℚ_p complete algebraically closed, π_1((D̃*_C)^♦/ℚ_p^×) ≅ G_{ℚ_p}. The proof uses 𝒴_{(0,∞)}^♦ = Spa C_p♭ × Spd ℚ_p, so 𝒴_{(0,∞)}^♦/G_{ℚ_p} = Spd ℚ_p × Spd ℚ_p, and X_FF = 𝒴_{(0,∞)}/φ^ℤ.
items.note: VS1 (Drinfeld's lemma for diamonds) and RF1 (the diamond formulas for the curve). Same content as Theorem 1.2.2 and the case n = 2 of Theorem 16.3.1.

items.name: Definition 15.2.1 and Remark 15.2.2: the category of Banach–Colmez spaces
items.statement: For C/ℚ_p algebraically closed, the category of Banach–Colmez spaces over C is the thick abelian subcategory of pro-étale sheaves of ℚ_p-modules on Perfd_C (≅ Perf_{C♭}) generated by ℚ_p and 𝔾_{a,C}^♦; it contains nonsplit extensions of 𝔾_a by 𝔾_a, unlike rigid spaces in characteristic 0 (compare Milne's category of sheaves on perfect schemes generated by 𝔽_p and 𝔾_a).
items.note: Missing: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB3 constructs BC(ℰ) as section sheaves but not Colmez's abstract category; routed with Le Bras's Theorem 15.2.12 as a source of VB3.

items.name: Theorem 15.2.3 (Scholze–Weinstein, Theorem A over perfectoid pairs) and universal covers of p-divisible groups
items.statement: For a perfectoid Tate–Huber pair (R, R⁺) and a pseudouniformizer ϖ ∈ R⁺ dividing p, with A_crys(R⁺/ϖ) the p-completed PD envelope of A_inf(R⁺) → R⁺/ϖ, p-divisible groups over R⁺/ϖ embed fully faithfully into finite projective A_crys(R⁺/ϖ)-modules M with φ_M : M → M[1/p] (the crystal evaluated on A_crys(R⁺/ϖ) → R⁺/ϖ). Consequently, for the universal cover G̃ = lim_p G of a p-divisible group G over 𝒪_C with Dieudonné module M over A_crys(𝒪_C/p), G̃_C(R, R⁺) ≅ G̃(R⁺/p) = (M ⊗ B_crys⁺(R⁺/p))^{φ=1}; the logarithm gives 0 → ℚ_p → D̃_C → 𝔾_{a,C} → 0 (for G = μ_{p^∞}, Example 15.2.4: D̃_C(R, R⁺) ≅ B_crys⁺(R⁺/p)^{φ=p}, x ↦ log[x]).
items.note: Missing, with Theorem 12.1.5. VB3:positive-basic-examples plans the Lubin–Tate universal-cover calculation (FS II.2.1), which covers the μ_{p^∞} example but not Theorem A.

items.name: Theorem 15.2.5, Definition 15.2.6 and Proposition 15.2.7: Dieudonné modules over B_crys⁺, the relative curve and its diamond
items.statement: (FF18) Dieudonné modules (M, φ_M) over B_crys⁺ = B_crys⁺(𝒪_C/p) (finite projective, φ_M : φ^*M ≅ M) are equivalent to bundles ℰ on X_FF, with (M ⊗ B_crys⁺(R⁺/p))^{φ=1} = H^0(X_{FF,S}, ℰ|_{X_{FF,S}}) for affinoid perfectoid S = Spa(R, R⁺)/C. For S ∈ Perf, X_{FF,S} := 𝒴_{(0,∞)}(S)/φ^ℤ, 𝒴_{(0,∞)}(S) = S ×̇ Spa ℚ_p = {p ≠ 0} ⊂ S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p, φ acting freely and totally discontinuously (κ(x) = log|[ϖ](x̃)|/log|p(x̃)| with κ ∘ φ = pκ); it is a sousperfectoid adic space over ℚ_p, perfectoid after base change to any perfectoid K/ℚ_p, and X_{FF,S}^♦ ≅ S/φ^ℤ × Spd ℚ_p.
items.locator: Lecture 15, §15.2, Theorem 15.2.5, Definition 15.2.6 and Proposition 15.2.7, pp. 135–136
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine RF1 ('establish q-Frobenius action, wandering annuli and the adic quotient X_S = Y_S/phi^Z … Construct the diamond formulas'), VB1 (isocrystal-to-bundle functor) and VB3 (section sheaves).

items.name: Definitions 15.2.8 and 15.2.11 with Examples 15.2.9–15.2.10: the Banach–Colmez spaces BC(ℰ) and BC(ℰ[1])
items.statement: For a coherent sheaf ℰ on X_FF whose torsion-free quotient has nonnegative slopes, BC(ℰ) : S ↦ H^0(X_{FF,S}, ℰ|_{X_{FF,S}}); for a bundle with all Harder–Narasimhan slopes negative, BC(ℰ[1]) : S ↦ H^1(X_{FF,S}, ℰ|_{X_{FF,S}}). Examples: BC(O) = ℚ_p; BC(i_{∞*}C) = 𝔾_{a,C}; for 0 < λ = s/r ≤ 1, BC(O(λ)) is the universal cover of the simple p-divisible formal group of slope λ, representable by a perfected open ball, with 0 → ℚ_p^s → BC(O(λ)) → 𝔾_a^r → 0; for λ > 1, 0 → BC(O(λ−1)) → BC(O(λ)) → 𝔾_a^r → 0; BC(O(−1)[1]) = 𝔾_{a,C}/ℚ_p; BC(B_dR⁺/ξ^n) from B_dR⁺(R♯)/ξ^n (B_dR⁺(R) = W(R) in characteristic p).
items.locator: Lecture 15, §15.2, Definition 15.2.8, Example 15.2.9, Example 15.2.10 and Definition 15.2.11, pp. 136–138
items.note: VB3 ('Construct the sheaf of sections T ↦ H^0(X_T,E_T), beginning with the explicit positive line-bundle and Lubin–Tate universal-cover calculations … Negative H^1 spaces have their separate construction').

items.name: Theorem 15.2.12 (Le Bras): Banach–Colmez spaces are diamonds and coherent objects on the curve
items.statement: All Banach–Colmez spaces are diamonds, and the category of Banach–Colmez spaces is equivalent to the full subcategory of the derived category of coherent sheaves on X_FF of objects ℰ_{≥0} ⊕ ℰ_{<0}[1], with the torsion-free quotient of ℰ_{≥0} of nonnegative slopes and ℰ_{<0} a bundle with all slopes negative; in particular it depends on C only through C♭.

items.name: Example 16.1.1 and Lemma 16.1.2: failure and a criterion for the Künneth formula for π_1
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, π_1 is not invariant under base extension (Artin–Schreier: Hom(π_1(Spec R), 𝔽_p) = R/{f^p − f}, e.g. R = k[T]) and π_1(X × Y) → π_1(X) × π_1(Y) fails for R = k[T]. If X, Y are schemes over k with Y qcqs and X connected, and for all algebraically closed k′/k, Y_{k′} is connected with π_1(Y_{k′}) ≅ π_1(Y), then π_1(X × Y) → π_1(X) × π_1(Y) is an isomorphism.
items.note: GS.4 (the proof of Drinfeld's lemma, which rests on this permanence of π_1).

items.name: Definition 16.2.1, Remarks 16.2.2–16.2.3, Theorem 16.2.4, Example 16.2.5 and Lemma 16.2.6: Drinfeld's lemma for schemes
items.statement: For connected qcqs X_1, …, X_n over 𝔽_p with partial Frobenii F_i, (X_1 × ⋯ × X_n/p.Fr.)_fét is the category of finite étale Y → ∏X_i with commuting isomorphisms β_i : Y ≅ F_i^*Y and β_n ∘ ⋯ ∘ β_1 = F_{Y/X} (for n = 2 one β suffices); it is a Galois category with group π_1(X_1 × ⋯ × X_n/p.Fr.), and π_1(X_1 × ⋯ × X_n/p.Fr.) → π_1(X_1) × ⋯ × π_1(X_n) is an isomorphism (Drinfeld 2.1, L. Lafforgue, Lau, Kedlaya). (For X_i = Spec 𝔽_p the group is ℤ̂ × ℤ̂.) The key step (Lau 8.12): for connected X/𝔽_p and X̄ = X ⊗ k, π_1(X̄/F_{X̄/k}) ≅ π_1(X); finite étale covers of X are those of X̄ with F^*_{X̄/k}Y ≅ Y.
items.locator: Lecture 16, §16.2, Definition 16.2.1, Remark 16.2.2, Remark 16.2.3, Theorem 16.2.4, Example 16.2.5 and Lemma 16.2.6, pp. 141–142
items.note: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.4 ('Prove Drinfeld's lemma in the exact lisse/finite-rank setting first').

items.name: Theorem 16.3.1 and Lemma 16.3.2: Drinfeld's lemma for (Spd ℚ_p)^n
items.statement: π_1((Spd ℚ_p)^n/p.Fr.) ≅ G_{ℚ_p}^n. With X = Spd ℚ_p/F^ℤ and any algebraically closed nonarchimedean C/𝔽_p, π_1(X_C) ≅ G_{ℚ_p}: by Proposition 15.2.7 and Theorem 10.4.2, (X_C)_fét ≅ (X_FF^♦)_fét ≅ (X_FF)_fét, and the latter is (ℚ_p)_fét by Theorem 13.5.7.
items.note: VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories VS1 ('Establish Drinfeld's lemma IV.7 for the divisor/Weil-action applications, separating partial Frobenius descent from an arbitrary fundamental-group product claim').

items.name: Proposition 16.3.3, Remark 16.3.4, Lemma 16.3.5 and Proposition 16.3.6: Stein factorization and the Künneth formula for diamonds
items.statement: Let k be a discrete algebraically closed field and D, X → Spd k diamonds with D → Spd k qcqs, such that for all algebraically closed nonarchimedean C/k, D_C is connected and π_1(D_C) ≅ π_1(D). For Y = D ×_k X and Ỹ → Y finite étale there is a finite étale X̃ → X, unique up to unique isomorphism, with Ỹ → X̃ having geometrically connected fibres (a Stein factorization); if moreover D and X are connected then D ×_k X is connected and π_1(D ×_k X) ≅ π_1(D) × π_1(X). The proof uses that at a geometric point Spa(C, C⁺) → X, 2-colim_{U ∋ x}(Y ×_X U)_fét ≅ (Y ×_X Spa(C, C⁺))_fét and 2-colim U_fét ≅ Spa(C, C⁺)_fét (Scholze 2017, 11.23(i)).
items.locator: Lecture 16, §16.3, Proposition 16.3.3, Remark 16.3.4, Lemma 16.3.5 and Proposition 16.3.6, pp. 144–146
items.note: VS1 (Drinfeld's lemma for diamonds) and DiamondsAndVStacks D5 (the finite-stage étale comparisons of ECD 11.17–11.31).

items.name: Definition 17.1.1 and Remark 17.1.2: the v-topology on Perfd
items.statement: The v-topology on Perfd is generated by open covers and all surjective maps of affinoids: {f_i : X_i → Y} is a cover iff for every quasicompact open V ⊂ Y there are a finite I_V ⊂ I and quasicompact opens U_i ⊂ X_i, i ∈ I_V, with V = ⋃_{i ∈ I_V} f_i(U_i) (printed with I_U in the last two places, sourceIssues E5). By Proposition 4.3.3 v-covers are quotient maps on topological spaces (set-theoretic cutoffs as in Scholze 2017).
items.note: DiamondsAndVStacks D2 ('Construct … the v-site').

items.name: Theorem 17.1.3, Proposition 17.1.4 and Corollary 17.1.5: 𝒪 and 𝒪⁺ are v-sheaves; flatness over totally disconnected bases
items.statement: X ↦ H^0(X, 𝒪_X) and H^0(X, 𝒪_X⁺) are v-sheaves on Perfd, with H^i_v(X, 𝒪_X) = 0 and H^i_v(X, 𝒪_X⁺) almost zero for i > 0 on affinoids (Scholze 2017, 8.7, 8.8). For totally disconnected X = Spa(R, R⁺), any map (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) to a Huber pair and a pseudouniformizer ϖ, S⁺/ϖ is flat over R⁺/ϖ, faithfully flat if Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) is surjective (Scholze 2017, 7.23). Representable presheaves are v-sheaves.
items.locator: Lecture 17, §17.1, Theorem 17.1.3, Proposition 17.1.4 and Corollary 17.1.5, p. 150
items.note: D2 ('Prove that 𝒪 and 𝒪⁺ are …' sheaves for these sites) and D1 ('Prove automatic flatness modulo a pseudouniformizer for maps to a totally disconnected base, and faithful flatness for a surjective map of affinoids').

items.name: Proposition 17.1.6 and Corollary 17.1.7: diamonds are v-sheaves, and v-descent of affinoid perfectoids over totally disconnected bases
items.statement: Every diamond is a v-sheaf (Scholze 2017, 11.9). X ↦ {Y/X affinoid perfectoid} is a v-stack on totally disconnected affinoid perfectoid X (Scholze 2017, 9.3).
items.note: D4 ('Prove diamonds are v-sheaves') and D3 (effectivity of descent over totally disconnected bases).

items.name: Lemma 17.1.8 and Corollary 17.1.9: v-descent of vector bundles and of bundles on B_dR⁺/ξ^n
items.statement: X ↦ {locally finite free 𝒪_X-modules} is a v-stack on Perfd; for n ≥ 1 including n = ∞, S = Spa(R, R⁺) ↦ {vector bundles on B_dR⁺(R♯)/ξ^n} is a v-stack.
items.note: RF2:integral-divisors ('v-descent for bundles on that divisor and its infinitesimal thickenings') and VB1 ('Prove rational/pro-étale/v descent in the exact source scope').

items.name: Definitions 17.2.1 and 17.2.3 with Proposition 17.2.2: small v-sheaves and their underlying spaces
items.statement: A v-sheaf F on Perf is small if it admits a surjection X → F from a perfectoid space. For small F and a surjection X → F from a diamond, R = X ×_F X is a diamond and F = X/R (Scholze 2017, 12.3); |F| := |X|/|R|, well defined and functorial by Proposition 4.3.3 (Scholze 2017, 12.7).
items.locator: Lecture 17, §17.2, Definition 17.2.1, Proposition 17.2.2 and Definition 17.2.3, p. 152
items.note: D4 ('Define small v-sheaves and small v-stacks with their atlas/relation smallness conditions, and prove their closure and topological comparison results, ECD §12').

items.name: Definition 17.3.1, Remark 17.3.2 and Example 17.3.3: spatial and locally spatial v-sheaves
items.statement: A v-sheaf F is spatial if it is qcqs and |F| has a basis of |G| for quasicompact open G ⊂ F; locally spatial if covered by spatial open subsheaves. For algebraic spaces qcqs implies the basis condition, but not for small v-sheaves or diamonds; quasicompact F has quasicompact |F| (converse for locally spatial F, Scholze 2017, 12.14(iii)); subsheaves of quasiseparated F are quasiseparated. Spa K/Frob^ℤ (one point) is not quasiseparated, while its product with Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) is spatial.
items.locator: Lecture 17, §17.3, Definition 17.3.1, Remark 17.3.2 and Example 17.3.3, pp. 152–153
items.note: D5 ('Define spatial and locally spatial diamonds by the sheaf-theoretic qcqs and qc-open-basis conditions, not just by the spectrality of the underlying space').

items.name: Propositions 17.3.4–17.3.5, Remark 17.3.6 and Corollary 17.3.7: spectrality of spatial v-sheaves and spectral quotients
items.statement: For spatial F, |F| is spectral and |X| → |F| is spectral for any perfectoid X → F (Scholze 2017, 12.13). For a spectral space X and a spectral equivalence relation R ⊂ X × X with open spectral projections, X/R is spectral and X → X/R spectral (Scholze 2017, 2.10); without openness any compact Hausdorff space arises from profinite X, R, giving qcqs diamonds with arbitrary compact Hausdorff |D|. A small v-sheaf with a presentation R ⇉ X by spatial v-sheaves with open projections is spatial.
items.locator: Lecture 17, §17.3, Proposition 17.3.4, Proposition 17.3.5, Remark 17.3.6 and Corollary 17.3.7, pp. 153–154
items.note: D5 (structural results of ECD §12) and D0 ('quotient criteria of ECD §2 … Prove the exact quotient hypotheses rather than the false assertion that every quotient of a spectral space is spectral').

items.name: Proposition 17.3.8 and Theorem 17.3.9: diamonds of qcqs analytic adic spaces are spatial; the spatial criterion for diamonds
items.statement: For a qcqs analytic adic space X over Spa ℤ_p, X^♦ is spatial. A spatial v-sheaf F is a diamond if every x ∈ |F| lies in the image of |X_x| → |F| for some quasi-pro-étale X_x → F from a perfectoid space (Scholze 2017, 12.18).
items.note: D5 ('Prove the spatial v-sheaf criterion of 12.18–12.21, which starts with point-surjectivity of a quasi-pro-étale map and concludes existence of an actual atlas') and D6.

items.name: Lemma 17.4.1 and Definitions 17.4.2–17.4.3 with Proposition 17.4.4: injections, closed immersions and separated maps of small v-sheaves
items.statement: For f : G → F of small v-sheaves, qcqs or with G, F locally spatial, TFAE: f is injective; f is injective on (C, C⁺)-points, C algebraically closed; |G| → |F| is injective and G = F ×_{|F|} |G| (Scholze 2017, 12.15). f is a closed immersion if it is quasicompact, injective and |G| → |F| is a closed immersion (for affinoid perfectoids this need not make R → S surjective, i.e. need not be Zariski closed); f is separated if Δ_f is a closed immersion (Scholze 2017, 10.7), iff f is quasiseparated and for every perfectoid affinoid field (K, K⁺) a map Spa(K, 𝒪_K) → G over Spa(K, K⁺) → F extends in at most one way (10.9).
items.locator: Lecture 17, §17.4, Lemma 17.4.1, Definition 17.4.2, Definition 17.4.3 and Proposition 17.4.4, pp. 155–156
items.note: D5 (representability and injectivity in §13), D3 (morphisms of stacks), PerfectoidSpaces P4 node closed-immersion-vs-zariski-closed.

items.name: Definitions 17.4.5 and 17.4.7, Proposition 17.4.6 and Corollary 17.4.8: proper and partially proper maps of small v-sheaves
items.statement: f : G → F is proper if quasicompact, separated and universally closed (Scholze 2017, 18.1), iff qcqs and for every perfectoid affinoid field (K, K⁺) a map Spa(K, 𝒪_K) → G over Spa(K, K⁺) → F extends uniquely (18.3); f is partially proper if quasiseparated and for every affinoid perfectoid Spa(R, R⁺), maps Spa(R, R°) → G over Spa(R, R⁺) → F extend uniquely (18.4). Hence f is proper iff partially proper and quasicompact, and f is a closed immersion iff proper and injective on (C, 𝒪_C)-points for algebraically closed C of characteristic p.
items.locator: Lecture 17, §17.4, Definition 17.4.5, Proposition 17.4.6, Definition 17.4.7 and Corollary 17.4.8, pp. 156–157
items.note: DiamondEtaleCohomology C4 ('Build ECD §18 on D5's small-v-stack geometry. Define properness, prove the valuative criteria'); AdicSpacesPartII R0 nodes universally-closed-morphism, partially-proper-morphism, proper-iff-partially-proper-quasi-compact, separated-proper-partially-proper and universally-specializing-morphism; AdicEtaleGeometry A2 node supplier-contract-separated-proper-smooth; PerfectoidSpaces P4 node separated-unique-extension-from-rank-one-locus.

items.name: Lemma 17.4.9 and Corollary 17.4.10: surjections and isomorphisms tested on geometric points
items.statement: If f : G → F of small v-sheaves is a surjection of v-sheaves then |G| → |F| is a quotient map; conversely, if f is quasicompact and |G| → |F| surjective (e.g. surjective on (C, C⁺)-points) then f is v-surjective (Scholze 2017, 12.11). A qcqs f is an isomorphism iff G(C, C⁺) → F(C, C⁺) is bijective for all affinoid fields (C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed (12.5).
items.note: D4/D5 (the small v-sheaf structure results of ECD §12).

items.name: Definition 17.5.1 (Appendix to Lecture 17): integral perfectoid rings and A_crys(R)
items.statement: An integral perfectoid ring is a p-complete ℤ_p-algebra R with Frobenius surjective on R/p, some π ∈ R with π^p = pu for a unit u, and ker(θ : A_inf(R) = W(R♭) → R) principal (R♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} R); so R = A_inf(R)/ξ with ξ a nonzerodivisor (BMS 3.10). A_crys(R) is the p-adic completion of the PD thickening of A_inf(R) → R; A_inf(R) → A_crys(R) is injective, and if pR = 0 (ξ = p) A_crys(R) has extra divided powers of p and is not p-torsion free, with a section A_crys(R) → A_inf(R).
items.note: PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra ('Construct integral perfectoid rings in the scope of BS22 … and the necessary A_inf/θ descriptions').

items.name: Theorem 17.5.2 (Appendix to Lecture 17): Dieudonné theory over integral perfectoid rings
items.statement: For an integral perfectoid ring R, p-divisible groups over R are equivalent to finite projective A_inf(R)-modules M with a φ-linear isomorphism φ_M : M[1/ξ] ≅ M[1/φ(ξ)] such that M ⊂ φ_M(M) ⊂ φ(ξ)^{-1}M. The equivalence is functorial in R, agrees with Dieudonné theory if pR = 0 and with Theorem 14.4.1 if R = 𝒪_C (which characterizes it), and M ⊗_{A_inf(R)} A_crys(R) is the Dieudonné module of G on the PD thickening A_crys(R) → R, compatibly with φ_M (covariant normalization, differing by p^{-1} from the usual one in characteristic p). Proved by v-descent in perfect schemes (Bhatt–Scholze); for p ≠ 2 also Lau, via displays.

items.name: Lemma 18.1.1 and Lemma 18.1.2: v-sheaves of pre-adic spaces, and Spd 𝒪_K = Spd 𝒪_C/G_K
items.statement: For any pre-adic space X over ℤ_p (not necessarily analytic), X^♦ (untilts T♯ with maps T♯ → X) is a v-sheaf. For a complete nonarchimedean K with p topologically nilpotent, completed algebraic closure C and G_K = Gal, Spd 𝒪_C → Spd 𝒪_K is a proper v-cover and Spd 𝒪_C/G_K ≅ Spd 𝒪_K.

items.name: Example 18.2.1 and Proposition 18.2.2: the underlying space of X^♦ for non-analytic X
items.statement: For a pre-adic space X over Spa ℤ_p there is a natural continuous surjection |X^♦| → |X|; |X^♦| is not described in general (its points are equivalence classes of maps Spa(L, L⁺) → X^ad from perfectoid fields). For X = Spa(𝔽_p[t], 𝔽_p[t]) the subfunctor R ↦ R°° ⊂ R⁺ is open in |X^♦| (the open disc inside the closed disc after base change to a field) but does not come from an open subscheme.

items.name: Proposition 18.3.1 and Lemma 18.3.2: full faithfulness on perfect schemes
items.statement: For a scheme X of characteristic p, X^♦ = (X^perf)^♦, and X ↦ X^♦ is fully faithful from perfect schemes of characteristic p to small v-sheaves on Perf. The proof uses: for a valuation ring V, a quasicompact Z and a continuous Z → Spec V, the image has a unique minimal point.

items.name: Proposition 18.4.1, Theorem 18.4.2 (Lourenço) and Remark 18.4.3: full faithfulness on flat normal formal schemes
items.statement: Let E/ℚ_p be complete and discretely valued with perfect residue field k. X ↦ X^♦ is fully faithful from flat normal formal schemes locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E to small v-sheaves over Spd O_E. For k algebraically closed, let C_{O_E} be the category of triples (X_η, X_s, sp) with X_η a rigid space over E, X_s a perfect scheme over k and sp : |X_η| → X_s(k) a map on classical points; then 𝔛 ↦ (𝔛_η, (𝔛_red)^perf, sp) is fully faithful on the same class (Lourenço), because for Spf R ⊂ 𝔛, R is the ring of power-bounded functions on (Spf R)_η (a Riemann Hebbarkeitssatz; also de Jong). Proposition 18.4.1 follows by recovering X_η from Y_η via Proposition 10.2.3, (𝔛_red)^perf from the closed complement of the maximal diamond open Y_a via Proposition 18.3.1, and sp from closures of classical points.

items.name: Definition 19.1.1, Proposition 19.1.2 and Remark 19.1.3: the B_dR⁺-affine Grassmannian
items.statement: For C/ℚ_p algebraically closed nonarchimedean and a reductive G/C, Gr_G = Gr_G^{B_dR⁺} is the étale sheafification of S = Spa(R, R⁺) ∈ Perf with untilt (R♯, R♯⁺) over (C, 𝒪_C) ↦ G(B_dR(R♯))/G(B_dR⁺(R♯)); LG and L⁺G send S to G(B_dR(R♯)) and G(B_dR⁺(R♯)), and Gr_G = LG/L⁺G. Equivalently Gr_G(S) is the set of G-torsors on Spec B_dR⁺(R♯) with a trivialization over Spec B_dR(R♯), or (for any open U ⊂ Spa C♭ ×̇ Spa ℤ_p containing Spa C, p invertible) G-torsors on the pullback of U to S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p trivialized off S♯ meromorphically along S♯ (G-torsors taken as exact ⊗-functors Rep_C G → bundles, glued by Beauville–Laszlo); Gr_G is a small v-sheaf.

items.name: Lemmas 19.1.4–19.1.5: Gr_G is separated and partially proper, and closed embeddings of groups give closed embeddings
items.statement: Gr_G is separated in the sense of Scholze 2017 (10.7), so Gr_G → Spd C is separated and quasiseparated, and it is partially proper; for a closed embedding G ↪ H of reductive groups, Gr_G → Gr_H is a closed embedding.

items.name: Proposition 19.2.1, Definition 19.2.2, Proposition 19.2.3 and Theorem 19.2.4: Schubert cells and Schubert varieties
items.statement: L⁺G(C) acts on Gr_G(C) with Gr_G(C) = ⨆_{μ ∈ X_*(T)⁺} G(B_dR⁺(C)) · ξ^μ (ξ^μ the image of μ(ξ)). For dominant μ, Gr_μ ⊂ Gr_{≤μ} ⊂ Gr_G are the subfunctors whose geometric points lie in L⁺G · ξ^μ, resp. ⨆_{μ′ ≤ μ} L⁺G · ξ^{μ′} (Bruhat order: μ − μ′ a nonnegative integral sum of positive coroots). Gr_{≤μ} is a closed subfunctor proper over Spd C, Gr_μ ⊂ Gr_{≤μ} is open, and Gr_{≤μ} is a spatial diamond.

items.name: Definition 19.3.1 and Lemmas 19.3.2–19.3.7: the Demazure resolution, and the proof that Schubert varieties are spatial diamonds
items.statement: For G = GL_n and μ = (k_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_n ≥ 0), G̃r_μ sends (R, R⁺) with untilt R♯ over C to chains of B_dR⁺(R♯)-lattices M_{k_1} ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ M_0 = B_dR⁺(R♯)^n with ξM_i ⊂ M_{i+1} ⊂ M_i and M_i/M_{i+1} finite projective of rank j_i over R♯ (k_{j_i} > i ≥ k_{j_i+1}): a succession of Grassmannian bundles and a spatial diamond. M_• ↦ (M_{k_1} ⊂ M_0) factors over Gr_{≤μ}, is v-surjective onto it and an isomorphism over Gr_μ, so Gr_μ is a locally spatial diamond. For μ = (N, 0, …, 0): X(R, R⁺) = {A ∈ M_r(W(R⁺)) : det A ∈ ξ^N W(R⁺)^×} is affinoid perfectoid, λ : X → Gr_{≤μ} is v-surjective, and (A, B) ↦ (A, BA) identifies X ×_{Spd C} L⁺_W GL_r with X ×_{Gr_{≤μ}} X, whose projections are open; Corollary 17.3.7 and Theorem 17.3.9 then give Theorem 19.2.4.

items.name: Definition 19.4.1 and Proposition 19.4.2: the Bialynicki-Birula map, an isomorphism for minuscule μ
items.statement: P_μ ⊂ G is the parabolic containing the Borel opposite to B with Levi the centralizer of μ, equivalently P_μ = {g : lim_{t→∞} μ(t)gμ(t)^{-1} exists}; Fℓ_{G,μ} = G/P_μ. There is a natural Bialynicki-Birula map π_μ : Gr_μ → Fℓ_{G,μ}^♦, an isomorphism if μ is minuscule (Caraiani–Scholze 3.4.3, 3.4.5; here via Corollary 17.4.10).

items.name: Theorem 19.5.1 (Appendix to Lecture 19): geometric, cohomological and Tannakian G-torsors on schemes
items.statement: For a flat affine group scheme G over ℤ_p and a scheme X over ℤ_p, geometric G-torsors, cohomological (fppf sheaf) G-torsors and exact ⊗-functors Rep G → Bun(X) are canonically equivalent (Saavedra Rivano, Broshi), via sections, pushouts Q ×^G (V ⊗ 𝒪_X), and the relative spectrum of P(𝒪_G(G)) (extended to ind-objects); for smooth G the étale site may replace the fppf site.

items.name: Theorem 19.5.2 and Proposition 19.5.3 (Appendix to Lecture 19): G-torsors on sousperfectoid spaces and their v-descent
items.statement: On a sousperfectoid adic space X the three kinds of G-torsors are equivalent (for affinoid X = Spa(R, R⁺), P(𝒪_G(G)) is a faithfully flat R-algebra whose analytified spectrum is a geometric torsor), and a geometric G-torsor is itself sousperfectoid, locally étale over a ball over X. For S ∈ Perf and an open U ⊂ S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p, S′ ↦ {G-torsors on U ×_{S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p} (S′ ×̇ Spa ℤ_p)} is a v-stack on Perf_S.

items.name: Definitions 20.1.1 and 20.1.3, Remark 20.1.2 and Proposition 20.1.4: convolution Grassmannians and convolution Schubert varieties
items.statement: G̃r^m_G/Spd C parametrizes G-torsors P_1, …, P_m over Spec B_dR⁺(R♯) with P_1 trivialized over B_dR(R♯) and P_i ≅ P_{i−1} over B_dR(R♯); G̃r^m_G ≅ ∏^m Gr_G over Spd C, a partially proper small v-sheaf. For μ_1, …, μ_m ∈ X_*(T)⁺, G̃r_{G,≤μ•} is the closed subfunctor where the relative position of P_i and P_{i−1} is ≤ μ_i at geometric rank-1 points (P_0 trivial); it is a spatial diamond proper over Spd C, and (P_i) ↦ P_m maps it v-surjectively onto Gr_{G,≤|μ•|}, |μ•| = Σμ_i.

items.name: Definition 20.2.1 and Propositions 20.2.2–20.2.3: the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian over Spd ℚ_p and its Schubert varieties
items.statement: For G reductive over ℚ_p, Gr_{G,Spd ℚ_p}(S) is the set of characteristic-0 untilts S♯ with a G-torsor on S ×̇ Spa ℚ_p trivialized off S♯ meromorphically along S♯; it is a small v-sheaf, the étale sheafification of S ↦ G(B_dR(R♯))/G(B_dR⁺(R♯)), and its base change to Spd C is the Gr_G of Lecture 19. For μ defined over E, Gr_{G,Spd E,≤μ} is a spatial diamond proper over Spd E, and for minuscule μ, Gr_{G,Spd E,≤μ} = Gr_{G,Spd E,μ} = Fℓ_{G,μ}^♦.

items.name: Definitions 20.3.1 and 20.3.3, Proposition 20.3.2 and Theorem 20.3.4: the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian over Spd ℤ_p and the Witt vector affine Grassmannian
items.statement: For a smooth model 𝒢 of G over ℤ_p, Gr_{𝒢,Spd ℤ_p}(S) is the set of untilts S♯ with a 𝒢-torsor on S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p trivialized off S♯ meromorphically; it is a small v-sheaf, the étale sheafification of G(B_dR(R♯))/𝒢(B_dR⁺(R♯)), with B_dR⁺(R♯) = W(R) on the special fibre. The Witt vector affine Grassmannian Gr^W_𝒢 on perfect 𝔽_p-schemes sends Spec R to 𝒢-torsors on Spec W(R) trivialized over W(R)[1/p] (the étale sheafification of R ↦ G(W(R)[1/p])/𝒢(W(R))); it is an increasing union of perfections of quasiprojective varieties along closed immersions (Bhatt–Scholze 9.6), so Gr_{𝒢,Spd ℤ_p} deforms Gr^W_𝒢 to the B_dR⁺-affine Grassmannian.

items.name: Definition 20.3.5 and Propositions 20.3.6–20.3.7: integral Schubert varieties for reductive models
items.statement: For 𝒢 reductive over ℤ_p and μ defined over E (unramified, residue field 𝔽_q), the Witt vector Schubert varieties are perfections of projective varieties, and Gr_{𝒢,Spd O_E,≤μ} ⊂ Gr_{𝒢,Spd O_E} (relative position ≤ μ at geometric rank-1 points) is a closed immersion with Gr_{𝒢,Spd O_E,≤μ} → Spd O_E proper and representable in spatial diamonds. For a closed immersion 𝒢 → ℋ of reductive groups over ℤ_p, Gr_{𝒢,Spd ℤ_p} → Gr_{ℋ,Spd ℤ_p} is a closed immersion.

items.name: Definitions 20.4.1–20.4.2 and 20.4.4 with Propositions 20.4.3 and 20.4.5: Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannians over (Spd ℚ_p)^m
items.statement: Gr_{G,(Spd ℚ_p)^m} sends S with m characteristic-0 untilts S_i♯ to G-torsors on S ×̇ Spa ℚ_p trivialized off ⋃S_i♯, meromorphically along this closed Cartier divisor; the convolution version G̃r parametrizes P_1, …, P_m with P_1 trivialized off S_1♯ and P_i ≅ P_{i−1} off S_i♯ for i = 2, …, m (printed '…, n' here and in Definitions 20.4.4 and 20.5.3, sourceIssues E6). Both are partially proper small v-sheaves. For μ_i over E_i, the Schubert subfunctors bound the relative position at S_i♯ by Σ_{j : S_j♯ = S_i♯} μ_j (resp. of P_i, P_{i−1} by μ_i). Then G̃r_{…,≤μ•} is a locally spatial diamond proper over ∏Spd E_i mapping v-surjectively onto Gr_{…,≤μ•}, which is proper, closed in Gr_{G,∏Spd E_i}, and a locally spatial diamond.

For 𝒢 reductive and μ_i defined over unramified E_i with rings of integers O_i, the Schubert variants over ∏Spd O_i: G̃r_{…,≤μ•} is representable in spatial diamonds and proper, maps v-surjectively onto Gr_{…,≤μ•}, which is proper, closed and representable in spatial diamonds over ∏Spd O_i.

items.name: Theorem 21.1.1, Remark 21.1.2 and Propositions 21.1.3–21.1.4: Witt vector affine flag varieties
items.statement: For 𝒢 over ℤ_p with reductive generic fibre whose identity component 𝒢° is parahoric, Gr^W_𝒢 is ind-proper (Zhu, for Iwahori; in general by lifting generic points to the Iwahori flag variety after extending the field), hence an increasing union of perfections of projective varieties. For a torus T with 𝒯 = 𝒯° the connected Néron model, Gr^W_𝒯 is the étale 𝔽_p-scheme of the Gal(𝔽̄_p/𝔽_p)-module π_1(T_{ℚ̄_p})_I. For parahoric 𝒢, π_0 Gr^W_{𝒢,𝔽̄_p} ≅ π_1(G_{ℚ̄_p})_I Frobenius-equivariantly via the Kottwitz map (Zhu 1.21); in general Gr^W_{𝒢°} → Gr^W_𝒢 is a π_0𝒢-torsor, π_0 Gr^W_{𝒢,𝔽̄_p} = π_1(G_{ℚ̄_p})_I/π_0𝒢_{𝔽̄_p}, and Gr^W_{𝒢°} → Gr^W_𝒢 is an isomorphism on connected components.
items.locator: Lecture 21, §21.1, Theorem 21.1.1, Remark 21.1.2, Proposition 21.1.3 and Proposition 21.1.4, pp. 191–192

items.name: Theorem 21.2.1, Theorem 21.2.2 (Anschütz) and Corollary 21.2.3: ind-properness of Gr_{𝒢,Spd ℤ_p}
items.statement: Gr_{𝒢,Spd ℤ_p} → Spd ℤ_p is ind-proper, an increasing union of closed subfunctors proper over Spd ℤ_p, and for a closed immersion 𝒢 ↪ GL_n the induced map to Gr_{GL_n,Spd ℤ_p} is a closed immersion. (Anschütz) For C algebraically closed nonarchimedean over ℤ_p, a 𝒢-torsor on Spec A_inf ∖ {𝔪} that is trivial on Spec A_inf[1/ξ] is trivial, hence extends (uniquely, by the Tannakian formalism and Lemma 14.2.3) to Spec A_inf; so every Spd C → Gr_{𝒢,Spd ℤ_p} given by a 𝒢-torsor over B_dR⁺(C) trivialized over B_dR(C) comes from a unique 𝒢-torsor over A_inf trivialized over A_inf[1/ξ].

items.name: Proposition 21.3.1: the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian of a torus
items.statement: Let 𝒯 be the connected component of the Néron model of a torus T, X the étale ℚ_p-scheme of the Γ-module X_*(T_{ℚ̄_p}) = π_1(T_{ℚ̄_p}), and X^int its normalization over ℤ_p (locally Spec O_K for Spec K ⊂ X), whose reduced special fibre is the étale 𝔽_p-scheme of π_1(T_{ℚ̄_p})_I. Then Gr_{𝒯,Spd ℤ_p} ≅ X^{int,♦} naturally over Spd ℤ_p.

items.name: Conjecture 21.4.1 and Remark 21.4.2: the Scholze–Weinstein conjecture on local models
items.statement: Let 𝒢 over ℤ_p have reductive generic fibre with 𝒢° parahoric, and μ a minuscule conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{ℚ̄_p} with reflex field E. There is a flat projective O_E-scheme M^loc_{(𝒢,μ)} with reduced special fibre and a closed immersion M^{loc,♦}_{(𝒢,μ)} ↪ Gr_{𝒢,Spd O_E} whose generic fibre is Fℓ_{G,μ}^♦ ≅ Gr_{G,Spd E,μ}. Such a scheme is normal (Serre's criterion) and unique if it exists (Proposition 18.4.1): its v-sheaf is the closure of Gr_{G,Spd E,μ}.

items.name: Propositions 21.4.3 and 21.5.1: local models are insensitive to π_0 and to central isogenies
items.statement: (21.4.3) For 𝒢 with connected generic fibre and 𝒢° parahoric, and minuscule μ over E, the closures Gr_{𝒢°,Spd O_E,μ} → Gr_{𝒢,Spd O_E,μ} of Gr_{G,Spd E,μ} ≅ Fℓ_{G,μ}^♦ are isomorphic. (21.5.1, Lourenço) For G̃ → G surjective with central kernel, 𝒢̃ a quasiparahoric model stabilizing a facet F of the Bruhat–Tits building and 𝒢 the quasiparahoric model of G fixing F, and μ̃ minuscule over Ẽ with image μ over E ⊂ Ẽ, the closures satisfy Gr_{𝒢̃,Spd O_Ẽ,μ̃} ≅ Gr_{𝒢,Spd O_E,μ} ×_{Spd O_E} Spd O_Ẽ.

items.name: Definitions 21.6.1–21.6.2, Remark 21.6.3, Theorem 21.6.4, Remark 21.6.5, Corollary 21.6.6 and Remark 21.6.7 (Appendix to Lecture 21): Rapoport–Zink lattice chains and their automorphism groups
items.statement: EL data: a finite-dimensional semisimple ℚ_p-algebra B and a B-module V (PEL: p ≠ 2, a nondegenerate alternating form with an involution b ↦ b* adjoint to it); G = GL_B(V), resp. the similitude group G(R) = {g : (gv, gw) = c(g)(v, w)}, assumed connected with F = Z(B) a field; a maximal order O_B and a periodic chain 𝓛 of O_B-lattices (Rapoport–Zink 3.1). A chain of O_B ⊗ R-lattices of type (𝓛) is a functor Λ ↦ M_Λ with periodicity isomorphisms θ_b, locally isomorphic to Λ ⊗ R with adjacent quotients locally Λ/Λ′ ⊗ R; a polarized chain adds an antisymmetric isomorphism M_Λ ≅ M*_{Λ*} ⊗ L for an invertible L (needed for the similitude factor). The automorphisms of 𝓛 (polarized in the PEL case) form a smooth group scheme 𝒢 over ℤ_p, chains of type (𝓛) are étale locally trivial (Rapoport–Zink 3.11, 3.16, stated there for p nilpotent in R), so 𝒢-torsors over R are chains of type (𝓛); 𝒢 need not have connected fibres, but 𝒢° is parahoric.

items.name: Definition 21.6.8, Proposition 21.6.9 and Corollary 21.6.10: the naive local model and its embedding into Gr_{𝒢,Spd O_E}
items.statement: For μ minuscule with weights 0, 1 on V (V ⊗ ℚ̄_p = V_0 ⊕ V_1, the opposite of Rapoport–Zink's normalization μ_RZ = χμ^{-1}) and, in the PEL case, c ∘ μ = id, M^{loc,naive}_{(𝒢,μ)} over O_E represents functors Λ ↦ t_Λ of O_B ⊗ O_S-modules finite projective over O_S with surjections φ_Λ : Λ ⊗ O_S → t_Λ compatible with periodicity, with det_R(a; t_Λ) = det_{ℚ_p}(a; V_1) for a ∈ O_B and (PEL) t*_Λ → Λ* ⊗ O_S → t_{Λ*} zero; it is projective over O_E. For a perfectoid Tate O_E-algebra R with a point (t_Λ, φ_Λ), M_Λ = ker(Λ ⊗ B_dR⁺(R) → Λ ⊗ R → t_Λ) is a (polarized) chain of O_B ⊗ B_dR⁺(R)-lattices of type (𝓛), giving a closed immersion M^{loc,naive,♦}_{(𝒢,μ)} ↪ Gr_{𝒢,Spd O_E} that is an isomorphism onto Gr_{G,Spd E,μ} on generic fibres.

items.name: Theorems 21.7.1 and 21.8.1 (Appendix to Lecture 21): the Rapoport–Zink and Kudla–Rapoport–Zink local model conjectures
items.statement: (EL, Rapoport–Zink 2017) For F/ℚ_p finite, D central division over F of invariant 1/n (n ≥ 2), B = V = D, 𝓛 = {Π^nO_D} (G(ℚ_p) = D^×, 𝒢(ℤ_p) = O_D^×) and μ as in RZ17, there is a natural 𝒢-equivariant isomorphism M^loc_{(𝒢,μ)} ≅ M^loc_Dr ×_{Spec O_F} Spec O_E with the Drinfeld local model. (PEL, Kudla–Rapoport–Zink) In the KRZ setting there is a natural 𝒢-equivariant isomorphism M^loc_{(𝒢,μ)} ≅ M^loc_Dr ×_{Spec O_{F_0}} Spec O_E, with the Drinfeld local model for F_0 and n = 2. No explicit map is known; the proof passes through the lifting of Proposition 21.5.1 (Remark 21.7.2).

items.name: Proposition 22.1.1, Definition 22.1.2 and Theorem 22.1.3: bundles on the relative curve as φ-modules
items.statement: For S ∈ Perf the following are equivalent: vector bundles on X_{FF,S}; φ-modules on 𝒴_{(0,∞)}(S); φ-modules on 𝒴_{[r,∞)}(S); φ^{-1}-modules on 𝒴_{(0,r]}(S). The relative Robba ring R̃_R = colim_{r>0} H^0(𝒴_{(0,r]}(S), 𝒪) carries φ as an automorphism, and bundles on X_{FF,S} are equivalent to φ-equivariant finite projective R̃_R-modules (Kedlaya–Liu).
items.locator: Lecture 22, §22.1, Proposition 22.1.1, Definition 22.1.2 and Theorem 22.1.3, pp. 207–208
items.note: VB1 ('Define bundles as finite locally free O_X modules on the existing curve; compare with finite projective modules on annuli and Frobenius descent') and RF1.

items.name: Theorem 22.2.1: upper semicontinuity of the Newton polygon (Kedlaya–Liu)
items.statement: For a bundle ℰ of constant rank on X_{FF,S}, s ↦ ν_ℰ(s), the Newton polygon (Harder–Narasimhan slopes by Theorem 13.5.4) of the pullback of ℰ to X_{FF,C} along a geometric point Spa(C, C⁺) → S over s, is upper semicontinuous on |S|.
items.note: VB4 ('Construct the geometric HN polygon of E_s, prove its semicontinuity with the source's dominance convention').

items.name: Theorem 22.3.1: bundles trivial at all geometric points are pro-étale ℚ_p-local systems (Kedlaya–Liu)
items.statement: 𝕃 ↦ 𝕃 ⊗_{ℚ_p} 𝒪_{X_{FF,S}} (descended by Proposition 19.5.3) is an equivalence from pro-étale ℚ_p-local systems on S to bundles on X_{FF,S} trivial at every geometric point of S (ν_ℰ ≡ 0).
items.note: VB4 ('Prove the equivalence between everywhere slope-zero bundles and pro-étale E-local systems').

items.name: Propositions 22.3.2 and 22.6.1: ℤ_p-local systems and G(ℤ_p)-torsors as φ^{-1}-modules on 𝒴_{[0,r]}(S)
items.statement: L ↦ L ⊗_{ℤ_p} 𝒪_{𝒴_{[0,r]}(S)} is an equivalence from pro-étale ℤ_p-local systems on S to φ^{-1}-modules on 𝒴_{[0,r]}(S) (equivalently, for affinoid S, φ-modules over the integral Robba ring R̃_R^int = colim_r H^0(𝒴_{[0,r]}(S), 𝒪)); restriction to 𝒴_{(0,r]}(S) corresponds to L ↦ L[1/p], so such modules have Newton polygon 0 on 𝒴_{(0,r]}(S) (Kedlaya–Liu). Likewise, for 𝒢 over ℤ_p, pro-étale 𝒢(ℤ_p)-torsors on S are equivalent to φ^{-1}-equivariant 𝒢-torsors on 𝒴_{[0,r]}(S).
items.note: Missing: VB4 plans the rational equivalence (Theorem 22.3.1); the integral version over 𝒴_{[0,r]}(S) and its 𝒢-torsor form are not planned. Routed as a source of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB4 with Theorem 12.3.4.

items.name: Corollary 22.3.3 and Theorem 22.6.2: the lattice functors Latt and the admissible locus
items.statement: For a φ^{-1}-module ℰ_η on 𝒴_{(0,r]}(S), Latt(ℰ_η) (S′ ↦ φ^{-1}-modules ℰ′ on 𝒴_{[0,r]}(S′) with ℰ′|_{𝒴_{(0,r]}(S′)} ≅ ℰ_η|_{S′}) is representable by a perfectoid space étale over S with image the admissible locus S^a ⊂ S where ν_{ℰ_η} ≡ 0; over S^a there is a ℚ_p-local system L_η and Latt(ℰ_η) parametrizes ℤ_p-lattices in it. For a G-torsor P_η on 𝒴_{(0,r]}(S) with P_η ≅ φ^{-1*}P_η, Latt(P_η) is representable by a perfectoid space étale over S whose open image is where ν_{P_η} and κ_{P_η} vanish; over it there is a pro-étale G(ℚ_p)-torsor, and Latt(P_η) parametrizes pro-étale 𝒢(ℤ_p)-torsors P with P ×^{𝒢(ℤ_p)} G(ℚ_p) = P_η.
items.note: Missing: the period-map/admissible-locus input for moduli of local shtukas (Proposition 23.3.3, Corollaries 23.4.4 and 23.5.3); routed as a source of HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas HS2.

items.name: Definition 22.4.1 and Remark 22.4.2: isocrystals with G-structure, B(G), and the Newton and Kottwitz invariants
items.statement: An isocrystal with G-structure is an exact ⊗-functor Rep_{ℚ_p} G → Isoc_k; trivializing the fibre functor (possible by Steinberg's theorem) gives b ∈ G(L), V ↦ (V ⊗ L, b ⊗ φ), changed by σ-conjugacy b ∼ φ(y)by^{-1}; B(G) is the set of σ-conjugacy classes, in bijection with isomorphism classes. Kottwitz's Newton point ν : B(G) → ((X_*(T) ⊗ ℚ)⁺)^Γ and κ : B(G) → π_1(G_{ℚ̄_p})_Γ give an injection (ν, κ) with known image, so B(G) is independent of k (in equal characteristic κ sends algebraic loops to topological loops). Composing with Isoc_k → Bun(X_FF) gives G-torsors on X_FF.
items.note: BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0 ('Define B(G) as sigma-conjugacy classes in G(E-breve) … compare with isomorphism classes of G-isocrystals') and BG1 (Kottwitz and Newton invariants).

items.name: Theorem 22.4.3 (Fargues) and Corollary 22.5.1: G-torsors on X_FF are classified by B(G), and ν is semicontinuous
items.statement: The map from B(G) to isomorphism classes of G-torsors on X_FF is a bijection. For a G-torsor P on X_{FF,S}, ν_P : |S| → ((X_*(T) ⊗ ℚ)⁺)^Γ is upper semicontinuous for the dominance order (from Theorem 22.2.1 and Rapoport–Richartz 2.2(iv)); κ_P should be locally constant (proved in Fargues–Scholze; a weaker version is proved below).
items.note: BG2:uniformization ('Prove the bijection |Bun_G| → B(G) … prove kappa locally constant … prove nu semicontinuous by faithful-representation HN theory').

items.name: Theorem 22.5.2: G-torsors trivial at all geometric points are pro-étale G(ℚ_p)-torsors
items.statement: Pro-étale G(ℚ_p)-torsors on S are equivalent to G-torsors on X_{FF,S} that are trivial at every geometric point of S.
items.note: VB4 (the rank-n case) with BG0's Tannakian comparison of torsors and exact tensor functors.

items.name: Definition 23.1.1 with Remarks 23.1.2–23.1.3: the moduli space of mixed-characteristic local shtukas Sht_{𝒢,b,{μ_i}}
items.statement: For 𝒢 smooth over ℤ_p with reductive generic fibre G and connected special fibre, b ∈ G(L) (L = W(k)[1/p], k = 𝔽̄_p) and conjugacy classes μ_1, …, μ_m of cocharacters of G_{ℚ̄_p} with fields of definition E_i (Ĕ_i = E_i · L), Sht_{𝒢,b,{μ_i}} → Spd Ĕ_1 ×_{Spd k} ⋯ ×_{Spd k} Spd Ĕ_m sends S = Spa(R, R⁺) ∈ Perf_k to quadruples (P, {S_i♯}, φ_P, ι_r): a 𝒢-torsor P on S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p, untilts S_i♯ over Ĕ_i, φ_P : Frob_S^*P ≅ P off ⋃Γ_{x_i}, meromorphic along ⋃S_i♯ and bounded at geometric rank-1 points by μ_• (as for Gr_{G,∏Spd E_i,≤μ•}), and ι_r : P|_{𝒴_{[r,∞)}(S)} ≅ G × 𝒴_{[r,∞)}(S) for r ≫ 0 identifying φ_P with b × Frob_S. Its isomorphism class depends only on the class of b in B(G).
items.locator: Lecture 23, §23.1, Definition 23.1.1, Remark 23.1.2 and Remark 23.1.3, pp. 216–217
items.note: HS2 node local-shtuka-moduli ('For b,b' in B(G) and a bounded tuple of modifications, define the local shtuka functor as the fibre of the Hecke correspondence over E_b,E_b', retaining trivializations').

items.name: Theorem 23.1.4 and Proposition 23.2.1: Sht_{𝒢,b,{μ_i}} is a locally spatial diamond; the case of no legs
items.statement: Sht_{𝒢,b,{μ_i}} is a locally spatial diamond (a v-sheaf by Proposition 19.5.3). With no legs, Sht_{𝒢,b,∅} is empty unless b is in the trivial class, and Sht_{𝒢,1,∅} is the constant perfectoid space G(ℚ_p)/𝒢(ℤ_p).
items.note: HS2 node local-shtuka-moduli ('prove diamond representability/local spatiality').

items.name: Proposition 23.3.1 and Corollary 23.3.2: one leg via the curve, and the duality isomorphism for basic b
items.statement: S-points of Sht_{𝒢,b,μ} are isomorphism classes of (S♯, ℰ, α, 𝒫): an untilt S♯ over E, a G-torsor ℰ on X_{FF,S} trivial at every geometric point, α : ℰ|_{X_{FF,S} ∖ S♯} ≅ ℰ_b|_{X_{FF,S} ∖ S♯} meromorphic along S♯ and bounded by μ, and a 𝒢(ℤ_p)-lattice 𝒫 in the pro-étale G(ℚ_p)-torsor of ℰ (Theorem 22.5.2). For basic b, with Ǧ = J_b (an inner form of G), b̌ = b^{-1} and μ̌ = μ^{-1}, there is a natural G(ℚ_p) × J_b(ℚ_p)-equivariant isomorphism Sht_{G,b,μ,∞} ≅ Sht_{(Ǧ,b̌,μ̌),∞} over Spd Ĕ.
items.note: HS2 (the Hecke-fibre description over ℰ_b and the trivial bundle, with J_b(E)-actions; the duality exchanges the two ends).

items.name: Proposition 23.3.3 and Remark 23.3.4: the Grothendieck–Messing period map is étale
items.statement: π_GM : Sht_{𝒢,b,μ,K} → Gr_{G,Spd Ĕ,≤μ} is étale; since Gr_{G,Spd Ĕ,≤μ} is a spatial diamond (Proposition 20.2.3), Sht_{𝒢,b,μ,K} is a locally spatial diamond.
items.note: HS2 ('prove diamond representability/local spatiality').

items.name: Definitions 23.4.1 and 23.5.1, Propositions 23.4.2 and 23.5.2, Remark 23.4.3: the twisted Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian Gr^tw
items.statement: For two legs, Gr^tw_{G,(Spd ℚ_p)²} is glued from the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian over (Spd ℚ_p)² ∖ ⋃_{n≠0}(φ × 1)^n(Δ) and pullbacks of the convolution Grassmannian under (φ × 1)^{−m} (m > 0) or the switch composed with (φ × 1)^m (m < 0), with Schubert varieties Gr^tw_{…,≤(μ_1,μ_2)}. In general Gr^tw_{G,∏Spd E_i,≤μ•} parametrizes G-torsors P_η on S ×̇ Spa ℚ_p with φ_{P_η} : Frob_S^*P_η ≅ P_η off ⋃S_i♯ (meromorphic), and ι_r identifying φ_{P_η} with b × Frob_S on 𝒴_{[r,∞)}(S), bounded at S_i♯ by Σ_{S_j♯ = S_i♯} μ_j (canonically independent of b); Gr^tw_{G,∏Spd E_i,≤μ•} → ∏Spd E_i is proper and representable in spatial diamonds.
items.locator: Lecture 23, §23.4, Definition 23.4.1, Proposition 23.4.2, Remark 23.4.3, Definition 23.5.1 and Proposition 23.5.2, pp. 221–223
items.note: HS0 ('Construct chains of modifications and identify composition over disjoint legs and over collisions with the convolution diagrams') and GS3:fusion.

items.name: Corollaries 23.4.4 and 23.5.3: étale period maps for several legs and the tower Sht_{G,b,{μ_i},K}
items.statement: There is an étale period map π_GM : Sht_{𝒢,b,{μ_i}} → Gr^tw_{G,Spd Ĕ_1 ×_k ⋯ ×_k Spd Ĕ_m,≤μ•}, whose open image is the admissible locus Gr^{tw,a}, carrying a G(ℚ_p)-torsor P_η, and Sht_{𝒢,b,{μ_i}} parametrizes 𝒢(ℤ_p)-lattices in P_η; so it is a locally spatial diamond depending on 𝒢 only through G and 𝒢(ℤ_p). For compact open K ⊂ G(ℚ_p), Sht_{G,b,{μ_i},K} parametrizes K-lattices, giving a tower of finite étale covers with Sht_{G,b,{μ_i},∞} = lim_K Sht_{G,b,{μ_i},K} a G(ℚ_p)-torsor over Gr^{tw,a}.
items.note: HS2 ('Define compact-open level quotients and the transition maps; prove diamond representability/local spatiality … Identify the tower as an inverse limit of level sheaves').

items.name: Definitions 24.1.1 and 24.1.3: local Shimura data and local Shimura varieties
items.statement: A local Shimura datum (G, b, μ) consists of a reductive G over ℚ_p, a conjugacy class μ of minuscule cocharacters of G_{ℚ̄_p}, and b ∈ B(G, μ^{-1}), i.e. ν_b ≤ (μ^{-1})^♦ and κ(b) = −μ^♮. Since π_GM : Sht_{G,b,μ,K} → Gr_{G,Spd Ĕ,≤μ} ≅ Fℓ^♦_{G,μ,Ĕ} is étale, Theorem 10.4.2 gives Sht_{G,b,μ,K} = M^♦_{G,b,μ,K} for a unique smooth rigid space M_{G,b,μ,K} over Ĕ étale over Fℓ_{G,μ,Ĕ}, with finite étale transition maps; the local Shimura variety is the tower (M_{G,b,μ,K})_K with its étale period map to Fℓ_{G,μ,Ĕ}.
items.note: HS2 ('Match the Hecke-fibre description with known local Shimura moduli in examples') with BG1 (Kottwitz and Newton invariants, the set B(G, μ^{-1})).

items.name: Proposition 24.1.2 (Rapoport): non-emptiness and B(G, μ^{-1})
items.statement: For C/ℚ_p complete algebraically closed and ℰ_b the G-torsor on X_{FF,C♭} attached to b ∈ B(G), there is a trivialization of ℰ_b|_{X_{FF,C♭} ∖ Spec C} with relative position μ at Spec C iff b ∈ B(G, μ^{-1}); hence Sht_{G,b,μ,K} ≠ ∅ iff b ∈ B(G, μ^{-1}).
items.note: Missing: BG1 defines the invariants but no layer plans this non-emptiness criterion (Rapoport's appendix to Scholze 2018); routed as a source of HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas HS2.

items.name: Definition 24.2.1, Theorem 24.2.2 and Remark 24.2.3: Rapoport–Zink spaces for GL_n
items.statement: For a p-divisible group 𝕏 = 𝕏_b over 𝔽̄_p of dimension d and height n, Def_𝕏 sends a formal scheme S/Spf Z̆_p to isomorphism classes of (X, ρ) with X/S a p-divisible group and ρ : X ×_S S̄ ≅ 𝕏 ×_{𝔽̄_p} S̄ a quasi-isogeny (S̄ = S ×_{Spf Z̆_p} Spec 𝔽̄_p). (Rapoport–Zink) Def_𝕏 is representable by a formal scheme 𝔐_𝕏 over Spf Z̆_p, formally smooth and locally formally of finite type (locally Spf Z̆_p[[T_1, …, T_m]]⟨U_1, …, U_r⟩/I), with all irreducible components of the special fibre proper over 𝔽̄_p.
items.locator: Lecture 24, §24.2, Definition 24.2.1, Theorem 24.2.2 and Remark 24.2.3, p. 226

items.name: Proposition 24.2.4 and Theorem 24.2.5 (Scholze–Weinstein): the generic fibre of a Rapoport–Zink space is a moduli space of shtukas
items.statement: 𝔐_{𝕏,Q̆_p} is the sheafification on CAff^op_{Q̆_p} (analytic topology) of (R, R⁺) ↦ colim_{R_0 ⊂ R⁺} Def_𝕏(R_0) over open bounded Z̆_p-subalgebras R_0 (SW13, 2.2.2). There is a natural isomorphism of diamonds 𝔐^♦_{𝕏,Q̆_p} ≅ Sht_{(GL_n,b,μ)} over Spd Q̆_p, μ = (1, …, 1, 0, …, 0) with d ones, at level GL_n(ℤ_p).

items.name: Definitions 24.3.1–24.3.3 and Proposition 24.3.4: EL and PEL Rapoport–Zink spaces
items.statement: For p nilpotent in R, a chain of O_B-p-divisible groups of type (𝓛) is a functor Λ ↦ X_Λ with O_B-actions and periodicity isomorphisms θ_b compatible with transitions, b acting as the composite for b ∈ B^× ∩ O_B normalizing O_B, and whose Lie algebras of universal vector extensions M_Λ form a chain of type (𝓛); in the PEL case add a ℤ_p-local system L and an antisymmetric X_Λ ≅ X*_{Λ*} ⊗ L. It is M^{loc,naive}_{(𝒢,μ)}-admissible if Lie X_Λ defines a point of the naive local model (the determinant condition det_R(a; Lie X_Λ) = det_{ℚ_p}(a; V_1)). For connected G, parahoric 𝒢 and b ∈ B(G, μ^{-1}) (slightly stronger than Rapoport–Zink's ν_b ≤ (μ^{-1})^♦), the Rapoport–Zink moduli problem 𝔐_D over Spf Ŏ parametrizes admissible chains with a quasi-isogeny to 𝕏_{b,Λ} modulo p (RZ96 3.21); 𝔐_D → ∏_Λ 𝔐_{𝕏_{b,Λ}} (already a large enough finite product) is a closed immersion, so 𝔐_D is a formal scheme locally formally of finite type over Spf Ŏ.
items.locator: Lecture 24, §24.3, Definition 24.3.1, Definition 24.3.2, Definition 24.3.3 and Proposition 24.3.4, pp. 229–230
items.note: Missing, with Theorem 24.2.2.

items.name: Corollary 24.3.5: EL/PEL Rapoport–Zink spaces are local Shimura varieties
items.statement: There is a natural isomorphism 𝔐_{D,Ĕ} ≅ M_{G,b,μ,𝒢(ℤ_p)} of smooth rigid spaces over Ĕ, identifying the natural 𝒢(ℤ_p)-torsors.

items.name: Definition 25.1.1: integral models of local Shimura varieties
items.statement: For a local Shimura datum (G, b, μ), a parahoric model 𝒢 over ℤ_p and the local model M^loc_{(𝒢,μ)} (Conjecture 21.4.1), M^int_{(𝒢,b,μ)} over Spd Ŏ sends S = Spa(R, R⁺) ∈ Perf_k to untilts S♯ over Ŏ with a 𝒢-torsor P on S ×̇ Spa ℤ_p, an isomorphism φ_P : Frob_S^*P ≅ P off S♯, meromorphic along S♯, and ι_r : P|_{𝒴_{[r,∞)}(S)} ≅ G × 𝒴_{[r,∞)}(S) (for an implicit pseudouniformizer) identifying φ_P with b × Frob_S, such that the relative position of Frob_S^*P and P at S♯ is bounded by M^loc_{(𝒢,μ)} (checked at geometric rank-1 points).

items.name: Theorem 25.1.2 and Corollary 25.1.3: comparison with Rapoport–Zink formal schemes
items.statement: For G = GL_n, μ = (1, …, 1, 0, …, 0) and b attached to a p-divisible group 𝕏 of dimension d and height n over 𝔽̄_p, with M^loc_{(GL_n,μ)} := Gr_{GL_n,Spd ℤ_p,μ}, there is a natural isomorphism 𝔐^♦_𝕏 ≅ M^int_{(GL_n,b,μ)} of v-sheaves over Spd Z̆_p; more generally 𝔐^♦_D ≅ M^int_{(𝒢,b,μ)} over Spd Ŏ in the EL/PEL situation of §24.3.

items.name: Proposition 25.2.1: integral models for tori
items.statement: If b = 1 and μ = 0 then M^int_{(𝒯,1,0)} ≅ T(ℚ_p)/𝒯(ℤ_p) as groups over Spd Z̆_p; in general M^int_{(𝒯,b,μ)}/Spd Ŏ is a torsor under M^int_{(𝒯,1,0)}.

items.name: Assumption 25.3.1 and Proposition 25.3.2: non-parahoric groups
items.statement: Assume H^1_ét(Spec ℤ_p, 𝒢) → H^1_ét(Spec ℚ_p, G) is injective (note H^1_ét(Spec ℤ_p, 𝒢) = H^1_ét(Spec ℤ_p, 𝒢/𝒢°)). Then the generic fibre of M^int_{(𝒢,b,μ)} is M_{G,b,μ,𝒢(ℤ_p)}.

items.name: Theorem 25.4.1, Lemma 25.5.1 and Theorem 25.5.2: the Rapoport–Zink and Kudla–Rapoport–Zink conjectures on Drinfeld-type formal schemes
items.statement: (EL, RZ17) For D as in RZ17 there is a natural J_b(ℚ_p)^1-equivariant isomorphism of formal schemes 𝔐^0_D ≅ 𝔐^0_Dr ×_{Spf Ŏ_F} Spf Ŏ_E with Drinfeld's moduli space. (PEL, KRZ) Assumption 25.3.1 holds (H^1_ét(Spec ℤ_p, 𝒢) → H^1_ét(Spec ℚ_p, G) is injective), and for D as in KRZ, 𝔐^0_D ≅ 𝔐^0_Dr ×_{Spf Ŏ_{F_0}} Spf Ŏ_E, where 0 marks the open and closed parts where ρ has height 0 and the Drinfeld space is for F_0 and n = 2. This proves the conjectures of Rapoport–Zink (2017) and Kudla–Rapoport–Zink, alternative moduli descriptions of Drinfeld's formal schemes proposed for a moduli-theoretic proof of Čerednik's p-adic uniformization.

routes.title: Prismatic cohomology: relative, absolute, Nygaard and log variants, Part II: prismatic Dieudonné theory
routes.brief: Coalesces with the candidate of the same id proposed by PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23 (and continued by PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-SCHOLZE-24 and PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24), whose final theorem is the classification of p-divisible groups over quasi-syntomic rings by admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystals. The Berkeley lectures supply the perfectoid and 𝒪_C cases, stated there as follows, and the design should prove them either as specializations of Anschütz–Le Bras (over an integral perfectoid ring admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystals are the modules below) or by the lectures' own route, recording which. Final theorems. (1) Theorem 17.5.2: for an integral perfectoid ring R (Definition 17.5.1, supplied by PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra), p-divisible groups over R are equivalent to finite projective A_inf(R)-modules M with φ_M : M[1/ξ] ≅ M[1/φ(ξ)] and M ⊂ φ_M(M) ⊂ φ(ξ)^{-1}M, functorially in R, agreeing with classical Dieudonné theory (covariant, normalized by p^{-1}) when pR = 0 and with (2) for R = 𝒪_C, and with M ⊗ A_crys(R) the crystal on A_crys(R) → R; the lectures prove it by v-descent in perfect schemes (Bhatt–Scholze) from (2). (2) Theorem 14.4.1 (the last part of Theorem 14.1.1): p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C are the minuscule Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules, equivalently pairs (T, Ξ) with T ⊗ B_dR⁺ ⊂ Ξ ⊂ ξ^{-1}T ⊗ B_dR⁺. (3) Theorem 12.1.5 (Scholze–Weinstein Theorem B): G ↦ (T_pG, Lie G ⊗ C(1)) is an equivalence with pairs (T, W), W ⊂ T ⊗ C, deduced from (2) and Remark 12.4.7; include Example 12.1.6 (d = 1, Drinfeld's Ω^h) with the corrected dimension formula (sourceIssues E1). (4) Theorem 14.4.2 and Theorem 15.2.3 (Scholze–Weinstein Theorem A): p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C/p, and over R⁺/ϖ for a perfectoid pair and ϖ | p, embed fully faithfully into finite projective A_crys-modules with Frobenius; with the universal cover G̃ and G̃_C(R, R⁺) = (M ⊗ B_crys⁺(R⁺/p))^{φ=1}. (5) Theorem 14.4.3 and Corollary 14.4.4: the crystalline Dieudonné module of G_{𝒪_C/p} is M ⊗_{A_inf} A_crys, and the special fibre corresponds to M ⊗ W(k); proved through Faltings' comparison (Proposition 14.8.1, Corollary 14.8.2, Proposition 14.8.3) and the reduction to formal abelian varieties with 𝔄[p^∞] ≅ G × G* (Propositions 14.9.3–14.9.4) and Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze's torsion-free comparison (Corollary 14.9.2). Imports: AInfCohomology AI.2 (Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules and Fargues' equivalence with (T, Ξ)) and AI.4–AI.5 (A_cris comparison, RΓ_{A_inf}); HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0/T2 (the Hodge–Tate map and sequence of Theorem 12.1.1); FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1–R07.2 (p-divisible groups, Dieudonné theory over perfect fields); CrystallineCohomology (crystals, A_crys); DiamondsAndVStacks D2 (v-descent) and GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0:Witt-geometry (v-descent of bundles on perfect schemes); AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli (formal abelian varieties, Serre duals). Tests: μ_{p^∞} and ℚ_p/ℤ_p, a height-2 dimension-1 group with W a non-rational line, étale and multiplicative groups over R with pR = 0, and the comparison of the two Frobenius normalizations.
routes.reason: The lectures classify p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C and over integral perfectoid rings by Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules and prove Scholze–Weinstein's Theorems A and B; the atlas plans Fargues' equivalence for BKF modules (AI.2) but no layer classifies p-divisible groups over these bases (T0 builds only the Hodge–Tate map, R07.2 works over perfect fields). routes.title: Pro-étale descent, diamonds and small v-stacks, Part II: recovery of integral models
routes.brief: Coalesces with the candidate of the same id from PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26 (continued by PAPER-GLEASON-LIM-XU-26), whose item I01 is Berkeley Proposition 18.4.1 and which asks for it with Scholze–Weinstein's own hypotheses; this route supplies Lecture 18 and its generic-fibre input from Lecture 10. Final theorems, as stated. Proposition 18.4.1: for E/ℚ_p complete discretely valued with perfect residue field k, X ↦ X^♦ is fully faithful from flat normal formal schemes locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E to small v-sheaves over Spd O_E. Theorem 18.4.2 (Lourenço), for k algebraically closed: 𝔛 ↦ (𝔛_η, (𝔛_red)^perf, sp) is fully faithful into triples (rigid space over E, perfect k-scheme, specialization map on classical points), via the Riemann Hebbarkeitssatz 'R = power-bounded functions on (Spf R)_η'. Proposition 18.3.1: X ↦ X^♦ is fully faithful on perfect schemes of characteristic p (with Lemma 18.3.2 on valuation rings), and X^♦ = (X^perf)^♦. Proposition 10.2.3: X ↦ X^♦ is fully faithful from seminormal rigid-analytic spaces over a nonarchimedean K/ℚ_p to diamonds over Spd K, and (Proposition 10.2.1, Lemma 10.2.2) universal homeomorphisms of analytic pre-adic spaces over ℚ_p induce isomorphisms of diamonds, 𝒪⁺/p^n being unchanged. The proof of 18.4.1 recovers X_η by 10.2.3, (𝔛_red)^perf from the closed complement of the maximal diamond open by 18.3.1, and sp from closures of classical points. routes.title: Geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve, Part II: integral local models

Final statements, as in the lectures. Conjecture 21.4.1 (Scholze–Weinstein): for 𝒢 over ℤ_p with reductive generic fibre and 𝒢° parahoric, and μ minuscule with reflex field E, there is a flat projective O_E-scheme M^loc_{(𝒢,μ)} with reduced special fibre and a closed immersion M^{loc,♦} ↪ Gr_{𝒢,Spd O_E} with generic fibre Fℓ^♦_{G,μ}; it is normal and unique (Remark 21.4.2, via Proposition 18.4.1). Proposition 21.5.1 (Lourenço): for a central isogeny G̃ → G and quasiparahoric models fixing a facet, the closures satisfy Gr_{𝒢̃,Spd O_Ẽ,μ̃} ≅ Gr_{𝒢,Spd O_E,μ} ×_{Spd O_E} Spd O_Ẽ. routes.title: The classical analytic cohomology inputs to diamonds, Part II: mod-p Poincaré duality for smooth proper rigid spaces
routes.brief: Coalesces with the candidate of the same id from PAPER-ZAVYALOV-25, which plans duality with p-torsion coefficients for smooth proper rigid spaces over C and needs the finiteness of their mod-p cohomology. This route adds the relative finiteness theorem of the appendix to Lecture 10. Final theorem, as stated: for C complete algebraically closed over ℚ_p and f : X → Y a proper smooth map of rigid-analytic spaces over C, R^if_*𝕃 is an étale 𝔽_p-local system on Y for every étale 𝔽_p-local system 𝕃 on X (Theorem 10.5.1), removing the extra hypothesis of Scholze's p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Theorem 1.10; the ℤ_p version follows.
